News.title: Terror trio including man who plotted to kidnap and behead soldier could be free within weeks
News.content:
THREE more dangerous Islamist terrorists — including one who planned to kidnap and behead a soldier — could be free within weeks after being granted parole hearings.

Parviz Khan, who got life with a minimum 14 years in 2008 for the plot, has won a hearing on September 29, which could see him released.



His trial heard he was claiming £20,000 in benefits a year while planning to seize a British Muslim serviceman and decapitate him “like a pig”.

He was jailed alongside four others, but the Leicester crown court trial heard that he was the ringleader of the Birmingham-based cell.



Khan, 55, was denied parole in 2022 after a board said he was “not suitable” for release.

Rangzieb Ahmed, an al-Qaeda operative once dubbed Osama bin Laden’s right-hand man in Europe, has been granted a parole hearing on August 20.

He was jailed in 2008 for setting up a terrorist cell in Manchester and was the first person to be charged with directing terrorism in the UK. His Manchester crown court trial heard he plotted mass murder, but he got a minimum term of just ten years.

Ahmed, 50, of Rochdale, was also denied parole in 2022, but has a new shot at freedom.



The third is Omar Khyam, of Crawley, West Sussex. He was part of an al-Qaeda cell that was jailed for plotting a series of attacks with fertiliser-based bombs.

Potential targets for “mass casualty” attacks included Bluewater shopping centre in Kent and London’s Ministry of Sound nightclub.

Khyam — linked to the July 7 London bombers — was jailed for conspiring to cause explosions, possessing 600kg of ammonium nitrate fertiliser for terrorism, and possession of aluminium powder.

Cell ringleader Khyam was told he must serve at least 20 years at the Old Bailey in 2007.

A year later he was handed another four-year term for throwing boiling oil over another inmate at Frankland Prison, Co Durham.



Khyam, 45, is due before a panel for a hearing on December 2.

It comes after we told on Monday how an al-Qaeda trio who planned to blow up transatlantic planes could be freed.

Terrorists Waheed Zaman, Arafat Waheed Khan and Ibrahim Savant, all of London, were jailed in 2010.

Ghaffar Hussain, an expert on radicalisation and former counter-terror officer on the Government’s Prevent programme, said: “These people all present massive risks and this is extremely worrying.”

The Parole Board said: “Decisions are solely focused on what risk a prisoner could represent to the public if released and whether that risk is manageable.”

News.title: Fury as mega-dinghies capable of carrying up to 230 migrants brazenly offered for sale online
News.content:
MEGA-dinghies like the one which took a record 230 migrants to Britain are sold brazenly online by Chinese factories.

The Sun found a 49ft boat for £1,400 in just five minutes on the Alibaba marketplace website.



We told how a similar inflatable, packed with more passengers than carried by an easyJet Airbus, was escorted to Dover after leaving Berck, in Northern France, on Sunday night.

Sun analysis revealed the migrants on that one boat alone could cost British taxpayers up to £25million.



The dinghy we found was listed by Qingdao Rongsheng Sports Goods Co Ltd as a “fishing and cargo boat” in the “waterplay crafts” section of China’s largest online shopping site.

The firm can also provide an engine, or a sample dinghy with a one-year warranty for a cut-price £1,270.



They offer boats in sizes starting at eight metres and boast a rating of 4.8 out of 5.

Another seller we contacted, the Qingdao Jiahai Boat Co, provides a “ten- metre sports yacht” for £860.

They said they would ship to European nations but, not which ones.

They insisted: “Our vessels are used for transporting goods.”



Many mega-dinghies are exported through Turkey and Bulgaria to Germany, and then on to northern France.

Rob Bates, of the Centre for Migration Control, told The Sun: “The work of people smugglers has never been easier.

“The Home Office has failed to deter migrants making the crossing, and we will now see an armada of these readily-available vessels.”



Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “An industry facilitating Channel crossings has sprung up.

Illegal immigrants are finding new ways to cross, and the mega dinghies show just how brazen this has become.”

French sea rescue charity SNSM said Monday’s boat had 260 people on board, but 30 were forced off because of the fear it would capsize.

Alibaba said: “We adhere to all applicable laws in the markets we operate in and require sellers to the same.

“Listings for boats and dinghies on our platform are intended for legitimate commercial uses such as fishing, cargo transport and marine operations.”



Additional reporting: Julia Atherley

News.title: Burnham doesn’t have the balls to deal with boats crisis, slams Farage after 230 illegal migrants arrive on mega-dinghy
News.content:
REFORM UK leader Nigel Farage has accused Andy Burnham of not having the balls to stop the boats.

The broadside came as the Prime Minister admitted he needs to change tactics to put a stop to the crisis.



Emerging from his week-long holiday, he conceded people will be worried by Monday’s arrival of a mega-dinghy carrying 230 illegal migrants.

Mr Burnham told GB News: “It shows that the gangs are changing their tactics, but so will we.”



Less than a fortnight after insisting the Government’s plan was working, he added: “We will now change our tactics and we will be relentless in chasing them down.”

But, in a Sun interview, Reform chief Mr Farage said: “Burnham has no more guts to deal with this than we had with Rishi, than we had with Boris Johnson.



“They tell the public what they want to hear. None of them have got the balls to actually deal with this. And I tell you what, I have.”

Ministers are scrambling to respond to public concern over the small boats crisis, which has resulted in asylum seekers being housed among worried communities.

More than 3,000 people have arrived in the three weeks since Mr Burnham entered Downing Street.

The recent surge has also sparked fury that French police are failing to make enough interceptions for the £1billion of UK taxpayers’ cash handed to Paris in recent years.



Home Office figures published on Tuesday revealed France stopped less than a third of those attempting to cross last week.

They thwarted 472 migrants launching from the beaches but 1,176 slipped through their fingers.

Pictures of gendarmes standing gormlessly while migrants storm into the sea have triggered calls to withhold some of the funding being given to France.



But Mr Burnham defended the arrangements, saying: “The deal we put in place, the payment by results deal, has created a change.

“There is more law enforcement on the other side of the Channel in summer 2026 than there was last summer, and that has led to quite a reduction in the number of crossings. But that’s not good enough.

“People will say to me, ‘We don’t want any crossings’. I understand that concern.

“There are further things that we are doing, and we will keep going at this issue until we deliver that eradication that people are looking for.”

He is understood to have kept Sir Keir Starmer’s target of closing every migrant hotel by the next general election.



Speaking in Clacton, Essex, ahead of tomorrow’s by-election there, Mr Farage repeated his plan to tow the boats back to France.

Quizzed on potential resistance from Emmanuel Macron’s government, the Reform leader told The Sun: “Well, give us our billion quid back then.

“We’ve given them a billion quid to stop the boats. The French navy literally escorts the boats to the 12-mile line and hands them over to the British authorities.



“Under the international rule of the sea, if people are in peril, and frankly anyone on those insecure boats is in peril, we are perfectly entitled to take them back to the safest next place of land, and that’s France — the safe country that they’ve come from.”

Mr Farage, who held a copy of Tuesday’s Sun with a photo of the mega-dinghy on the front page, added: “We’ve got a Royal Navy, we’ve also got a fleet of Border Force vessels there, based in Ramsgate, dealing with these operations.

“And frankly, if the Royal Navy is not there to protect us from invasion what’s the point of having it?”

He also warned that the deathtrap dinghies would lead to more tragedies in the Channel if they are not halted.

Mr Farage said: “I want to stop the boats to secure our borders.



ANDY: DO YOUR BIT By Jack Elsom MIDDLE-class families must “play their part” by accepting asylum seeker accommodation near their homes, the PM said yesterday. Fury has erupted in towns and villages where migrants have been dumped in hotels or houses of multiple occupation. But Mr Burnham said: “We cannot have a situation where it’s only the poorest communities that receive all of the dispersal of refugees and asylum seekers. “I believe all parts of the country need to play their part.” Asked if he would commit to stopping small boats by next parliament, he said: “It would be wrong to make a prediction. I promise a relentless focus on this issue.”

“I want to stop the boats in the interest of national security. I want to stop the boats in the interest of the safety of women and girls.

“But I also want to stop the boats to save lives, because people are dying, and those that come, many finish up working in criminal gangs, finish up, frankly, in the equivalent of modern-day slavery.

“We should be hanging our heads in shame over this.”

Meanwhile, Housing Secretary Angela Rayner has been accused of being in denial for saying the small boats are often packed with women and children.



She made the remark as she lashed out at smuggling gangs for piling desperate people into ramshackle dinghies.

Ms Rayner told the BBC: “We’re also saying that those criminal gangs that are putting often children and women into vessels that are not seaworthy, we’re seeing people that are dying at sea that are desperate to come here and we’ve got to crack that and stop it.”

Around three-quarters of small boat arrivals are men, according to Home Office figures.

Shadow Home Secretary Chris Philp said: “Angela Rayner is in denial. Illegal Channel crossings are dominated by young single males.

“Those women and children that cross are often being used as a human shield.

News.title: Heartbreaking 911 audio reveals desperate fight to save kids ‘killer mom Kailey Erhart stabbed’ after warning to husband
News.content:
A HARROWING race against time to save a mom’s three children after she allegedly slashed their throats has been captured in emergency dispatch audio.

Kailey Erhart, 22, has been charged with two counts of murder and one count of attempted murder after cops found her covered in blood and holding a knife to her throat.



Her three children were found unresponsive in a bedroom at a home in Mandan, North Dakota, with horrific neck wounds.

Erhart’s five-month-old and three-year-old daughters died, while her one-year-old son miraculously survived the attack.



The unthinkable tragedy has rocked the town with police saying the scene was one of the most horrific they had ever encountered.

Heartbreaking 911 dispatch audio, obtained by The U.S. Sun, reveals emergency responders were initially dispatched to the residence around 5:42 pm on Thursday, August 6.



A female operator is heard directing units to stage nearby for “a possible stabbing.”

Mandan Fire Department crews coordinated their approach before dispatch issued a grim update, ordering all responding units to proceed directly to the residence “for three children with cuts to their throats.”

One engine radioed in its initial assessment of the first child found, reporting, “We have lacerations… full front lacerations on the first kid, probably 1 to 2 years old, still breathing.”

Moments later, an officer updated dispatch on the full scope of the tragedy unfolding outside, revealing, “We have three infants, all with bad neck lacerations, out on the street, all still currently breathing at this time.”



Recognizing the extreme severity of the injuries, crews frantically requested air medical transport and additional fire personnel while scrambling to arrange emergency care.

Desperate to ensure the hospital was prepared for the incoming victims, a responder radioed dispatch, “Tell them that we have trauma… we need trauma surgeons. Just call them and tell them that. I don’t have time to call.”

Dispatch confirmed they would handle the alert, while officers rode alongside the victims in the emergency rigs to help maintain life support on the journey to the hospital.

The scale of the emergency was so vast that local crews were pulled from their stations, prompting off-duty EMTs to be called in to ensure Mandan still had enough personnel to respond to other 911 calls.

Cops say Erhart’s daughters died after the stabbings, while her son survived after having surgery.



Family told The U.S. Sun on Monday that he is expected to make a full recovery but declined to comment further on the tragedy.

According to court records and investigative affidavits, Erhart confronted her husband and the children’s paternal grandmother inside the home while holding one of her children and brandishing a handgun.

She allegedly told the father, “Say goodbye to your kids.”



He told police he managed to disarm her and disassemble the firearm, but Erhart allegedly then grabbed a kitchen knife, forced the adults out of the home and locked the doors.

Investigators later reportedly found video on the father’s phone that captured part of the terrifying confrontation.

The affidavit also details previous concerns over Erhart’s behavior, with her husband reportedly warning authorities that she had threatened to harm herself and the children.

Those concerns allegedly led to her admission to a mental health facility within the previous 12 to 18 months.

She was later discharged on medication and allowed to be around her kids, while Child Protective Services was allegedly aware of the previous threats.



After the attack, cops reportedly found Erhart in the kitchen covered in blood and holding a knife to her own throat.

She allegedly dropped the weapon before begging officers to kill her.

Erhart later reportedly told investigators she had put the children to bed and believed their throats had already been cut.

She claimed she could not remember what happened, but acknowledged she had been holding the knife when officers arrived, according to the affidavit.

Mandan Police Chief Jason Ziegler said the horrific scene would likely stay with the officers who responded.



“A scene like that is something that nobody should ever have to see, and the way [the officers] came through in one of the most horrific times that they’ll probably experience in their life. I’m proud,” Ziegler said during a press conference Friday.

He also acknowledged the devastating impact on the children’s family and others who were at the scene.

“I want to acknowledge this is an extreme, tragic and heartbreaking incident for the children involved, their families, our community and first responders who arrived on scene,” Ziegler said.



“Our thoughts are with everyone that were impacted by this tragic incident.”

Meanwhile, a chilling detail on Erhart’s Facebook profile has since emerged.

Her bio included the phrase, “Life’s a dance you learn as you go,” followed by a reference to 1 John 1:9.

The Bible verse reads, “If we confess our sins, he is faithful and just and will forgive us our sins and purify us from all unrighteousness.”

Erhart is facing nine criminal charges, including Class AA felony murder, attempted murder and aggravated assault.



Her bond was set at $3 million cash, with a judge citing the “extreme violence” alleged in the charges and the threat to the community, victims and children.

She has not yet entered a plea and is due back in court for a preliminary hearing and arraignment on October 6.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A GoFundMe launched by the children’s paternal grandmother has raised more than $30,000 as the devastated family grieves the loss of Erhart’s two kids and prepares for their funerals.

If you or someone you know is affected by any of the issues raised in this story, call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988, chat on 988lifeline.org, or text Crisis Text Line at 741741.

News.title: Reckless semi-pro footballer jailed after filming himself hitting 191mph on motorway and posting video on social media
News.content:
A RECKLESS boy racer has been jailed for hitting 191mph on a motorway.

Semi-pro footballer Connor Charlton filmed the speedo-meter in his souped-up BMW X3M and posted it on social media.



Another video showed him weaving in and out of traffic at 160mph in the £90,000 SUV.

The dad of two captioned it “wow” alongside a laughing emoji.



In further clips he hit 157mph as he sped from a red light, and a pal recorded him “drifting” round a roundabout.

In a spine-chilling near-miss, where Charlton pulled out in front of a white van, a person can be heard exclaiming: “Woah, woah, woah” before screeching with laughter.



His BMW was eventually seized by police after he was involved in a crash in September 2023.

The investigation revealed a note on his phone with a fabricated story about the collision — claiming it was another driver’s fault and that they had left the scene.

A search of the car’s computer found it recorded speeds of over 107mph eight times in a year.

Charlton, 32, was charged with ten dangerous driving offences and four of perverting justice for arranging for others to take penalty points for him.



He admitted all the charges at Leeds crown court.



It heard the Nostell Miners Welfare FC striker had two previous convictions unrelated to driving, including being found guilty of ABH in 2019 after punching a man during a five-a-side match in Wakefield, West Yorks.

Charlton, of nearby Hunslet, got four years’ jail and was banned from driving for four years and seven months.

News.title: Miss Universe host hits out at pageant on stage after contestants wore indigenous dress during competition
News.content:
A PAGEANT host has slammed two Miss Universe Canada contestants after they wore Indigenous-inspired outfits during the competition.

The controversy stemmed from a national costume segment days earlier, which former winner Ashley Callingbull described as cultural appropriation.



Callingbull, a Plains Cree woman from the Enoch Cree Nation, interrupted her co-host during the pageant’s final and said: “Sometimes there are mistakes that are made.

“It’s 2026. We should know better, but most importantly, a part of reconciliation is that we educate and learn and understand and move on from these things in a good way.”



She took issue with one contestant who wore a fur dress and boots, while another appeared on stage wearing a feathered headdress.

Speaking to CBC Indigenous, Callingbull said: “My jaw just dropped on the floor.



“This cannot be real. I just couldn’t get over that this was happening. Who allowed this on stage? Who approved this?

“Anything traditional or sacred should not be allowed. I was very, very upset.”



One of the controversial costumes, worn by Karisa Haverkemp, featured a feathered headdress traditionally associated with highly respected Indigenous leaders in North America.

She also had a red handprint painted across her face – a symbol of solidarity with the Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women and Girls (MMIWG) movement.

In a statement, Miss Universe Canada said: “If any costume caused offense, hurt or misunderstanding, please know it was never our intention.”

Haverkemp later took to Instagram to acknowledge her mistake.

She wrote: “I acknowledge and recognise that my outfit for the national costume caused hurt and offence to people in the Indigenous community.



“I appreciate what I have learned from this experience.”

The other contestant, Jasleen Kaily, wore a costume titled “Arctic Beauty”.

It featured an all-fur dress, fur boots known as mukluks, and two braids.



Kaily also apologised on social media, saying: “My intention was never to disrespect or misrepresent Indigenous culture” but rather to “recognise and celebrate one of the First Peoples of Canada”.

According to the Miss Universe Canada website, the national costume segment is “a celebration of Canadian culture and heritage, combined with creativity”.

It states: “Each delegate must showcase a unique costume, dress, or outfit inspired by Canada’s traditions, symbols, and history.”

The organisation has now said it will introduce a “comprehensive costume guide” to “establish clear guidelines and standards for all future pageant cycles to ensure every presentation is thoughtful and respectful”.

Pageant director Sonny Borrelli said he has also invited Callingbull to be the costume segment’s official liaison.



It is not the first time the Miss Universe Canada competition has faced criticism over cultural appropriation.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In 2015, the organisation said there had been a “misunderstanding” over entrant Paola Nunez Valdez, who wore a totem pole costume during the national costume segment.

Both Valdez and the organisation said the outfit was intended to represent her Dominican heritage.

News.title: Britain’s so hot that woman in Dorset has grown BANANAS – as UK on course for warmest summer on record
News.content:
BRITAIN’S blistering summer will see temperatures hit 38C tomorrow — with bananas among the few things growing.

Health warnings were issued, with householders told to close the curtains for extra shade during a fifth successive heatwave.



Experts predicted shortages of some foods in shops and higher prices as drought-hit farms battle to keep crops alive during what is set to be the hottest summer on record.

More expensive grain for animal feed will push up meat costs, and milk output has fallen as cows struggle in the heat and grass turns brown.



NFU president Tom Bradshaw added: “It does feel like there are going to be some shortages of food product.”

Analysts Shore Capital called it Britain’s “worst food security challenge in decades”.

But in Poole, Dorset, Pam Woodall found bananas growing on her garden fruit trees for the first time since she moved in 13 years ago.

The fruit typically grows in tropical climates in Asia and South America.

But Pam said she was shocked to see a bunch on her tallest 10ft plant.

She said: “I was walking around the garden and thought, ‘What’s that?’ It looks amazing but I’ll wait to see if the bananas ripen.”



Tomorrow’s 38C high would equal this year’s top temperature, recorded at Lingwood in Norfolk on June 26.

Extreme amber heat warnings have been issued for large swathes of England, including London, parts of the South East and East, the Midlands, and Yorkshire.

People are advised to keep out of the sun, drink lots of fluids — and close curtains.



The Met Office also warned the hot weather is likely to bring travel chaos and damage to heat-sensitive infrastructure — potentially causing power cuts in places.

Chief forecaster Chris Bulmer said: “High pressure is now becoming dominant and temperatures will build day-by-day. Southerly and south-easterly winds will also tap into the hot conditions over Europe.”

Up to 27million people are under hosepipe bans as reservoirs and rivers dry up, with increased risk of wildfires.

News.title: Dozens of police chiefs urge PM Andy Burnham to prevent PC Andrew Harper killers' early prison release
News.content:
Dozens of police chiefs urge PM Andy Burnham to prevent PC Andrew Harper killers' early prison release

Andy Burnham is 'increasingly confident' the killers of PC Andrew Harper will not be released early, but an open letter has demanded drastic changes and stronger protections

View 4 Images Greater Manchester Police Chief Constable Stephen Watson is one of dozens to sign the letter (Image: Adam Gerrard / Daily Mirror)

An open letter signed by 50 police and law enforcement leaders from across Britain has demanded PC Andrew Harper's killers remain locked up.

‌



In an unpresented move, dozens of high-ranking officers have written to the Prime Minister with three key demands, as Andy Burnham comes under increasing pressure from victims' families not to allow Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers - sentenced to 13 years for the cop's manslaughter in 2020 - to be freed in January.

‌



The new PM has ordered an urgent review into the controversial plan. A change was expected to sentencing rules from October 1, meaning most adults serving a standard prison sentence would be released earlier than the date originally set. Prisoners convicted of less serious offences were also expected to leave jail after a third of their sentence.

‌



4 View 4 Images PC Andrew Harper was killed back in 2019 (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire) 4 View 4 Images Andy Burnham is 'confident' the killers will remain behind bars (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News)

Should the early prisoner release scheme be paused? Take our poll and have your say READ MORE :

Andy Burnham confident release of PC Harper's killers will be blocked READ MORE :

Mr Burnham said he is “increasingly confident” the killers of PC Harper will not be released early, but that hasn't stopped the open letter being published. Greater Manchester Police Chief Constable Stephen Watson and Commissioner Pete O’Doherty were just two of the officials to put their name to it.

They asked the Government to consider three measures, and wanted every lawful option examined to determine whether the earlier release of those responsible for the PC's death could be prevented.

‌



They also wanted additional public protection safeguarding to be established in cases involving the most serious offenders whenever future changes to sentencing on release arrangements are considered.

Thirdly, they demanded victims and bereaved families must be "properly considered" whenever significant changes are made to sentencing or release arrangements.

View 4 Images The PM is under intense public pressure regarding the potential early release of Jessie Cole and Albert Bowers (Image: Thames Valley Police/PA Wire)

‌



Justice Secretary Alex Norris has been tasked by Mr Burnham with finding ways to keep the serious offenders in prison.

The letter read: "Dear Prime Minister, We welcome your intervention regarding the potential earlier release of those responsible for the death of PC Andrew Harper, and your instruction to the Justice Secretary to examine what can lawfully be done.

"When the state asks people to run towards danger on behalf of the public, they should be able to trust that the justice system will stand behind them when the worst happens. PC Andrew Harper's case also raises a wider question.

‌



"When someone is sentenced for an exceptionally serious offence, how much confidence can victims, bereaved families and the public place in that sentence if subsequent changes to release arrangements result in an offender being released significantly earlier than originally anticipated? This question extends far beyond policing.

"Families across the country are now facing the distress of learning that offenders may be released earlier than they understood when sentence was passed. We do not suggest that the grief of a police family is greater than that of any other bereaved family, nor that the life of an emergency worker has greater value.

‌



"Our concern is for all victims and families affected by serious offending sentencing changes. PC Andrew Harper lost his life while protecting the public and serving his community. Following his death, Lissie Harper campaigned for a change in the law, leading Parliament to establish Harper's Law, recognising the exceptional risks emergency workers take while protecting others.

"Police officers and staff see first-hand the impact serious crime has on victims and their families. They support people through some of the most difficult moments of their lives and ask them to place their trust in the justice system. That trust is vital and should not be weakened.

"We are also collectively concerned that an approach to early release which does not sufficiently distinguish the most serious offending risks undermining public safety, victim confidence and wider confidence in the criminal justice system."
