Temperatures are expected to soar to 36C for parts of England, hotter than Barcelona this week, as heatwave conditions return to many parts of the country.

Following a dry, sunny and warm weekend for many across England and Wales this weekend, parts of the country will be hotter than the Catalan tourist hotspot, which can only expect highs of 33C on Friday, while the Met Office has predicted temperatures will climb “significantly” across the UK this week.

Temperatures are expected to rise to 30C across parts of England and Wales on Tuesday, increasing to between 32C and 34C on Wednesday.

open image in gallery Temperatures will soar across the entire UK on Thursday ( Met Office )

While weather maps currently show peaks of 34C across the South East and East Anglia, the Met Office said temperatures are likely to rise to 36C in parts of those regions on Thursday.

Deputy chief forecaster Mike Silverstone said that the heatwave is expected to be fairly widespread across England and Wales, with Scotland and Northern Ireland experiencing high temperatures on Wednesday.

“Temperatures will climb through the weekend and, more significantly, through much of next week. After a brief dip on Monday, high pressure will move across the UK before settling to the east, allowing a southerly flow to develop,” he said.

“A fairly widespread heatwave is likely across large parts of England and Wales, with hot conditions developing in places. The heat is expected to peak for much of England, Wales, Northern Ireland and Scotland on Wednesday, with up to 34C possible in parts of central and southern England and southeast Wales. East Anglia and south-east England, however, could see temperatures even higher on Thursday.

open image in gallery Across England and Wales, the mercury is expected to surpass 30C on Thursday ( Met Office )

“Humidity levels are also expected to increase through the week, which may make conditions feel more uncomfortable, particularly overnight.”

The UK has experienced a consistent North-South split in the weather across this summer, with Scotland and Northern Ireland seeing heavy spells of rain over the weekend while almost three-quarters of England and the whole of Wales are now under drought, with emergency services warning of tinderbox conditions.

Nevertheless, temperatures are expected to reach 26C in Edinburgh on Wednesday, with Belfast seeing balmy 25C. Further south, temperatures will remain above 30C across England and Wales. The mercury is expected to peak at 30C as north as Leeds on Wednesday.

open image in gallery Yorkshire and the Humber, north-west England, the East and Eest Midlands, London, and south-east and south-west England are all under amber heat health alerts ( UKHSA )

These temperatures will stretch further north on Thursday with Newcastle-upon-Tyne experiencing 30C while Leeds and York experience scorching 33C heat.

Amber and yellow heat health alerts have been issued across England from 9am on Monday until 9pm on Friday, with the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) warning of adverse impacts on the elderly and vulnerable population and significant impacts across health and social care services.

While north-east England is under a yellow heat health alert, the rest of England has been placed under an amber alert with the watchdog warning of a rise in deaths, particularly among those aged 65 and over or with health conditions.

Met Office five-day weather forecast

Tuesday

A dry and sunny day for most with light winds. Cloudier in northwest Scotland and western parts of Northern Ireland with some outbreaks of light rain. Very warm in the sunshine.

Wednesday

Cloudy in western Scotland and western parts of Northern Ireland with showers, turning heavy at times. A dry and sunny day elsewhere with hot sunshine.

Outlook for Thursday to Saturday

Turning hotter through the next few days with extreme heat possible in parts of England and Wales, particularly on Thursday. Largely dry and sunny, but showers possible in the northwest.

Universal Studios Hollywood is set to install two additional sound barriers around its newest outdoor coaster following noise complaints from nearby residents, one of whom described riders’ screams as sounding like “bloody murder.”

The theme park’s upcoming attraction, Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift, features rotating vehicles moving at speeds up to 72 mph, which has brought intense reactions from people living in the adjacent Toluca Lake neighborhood. The ride is currently undergoing technical rehearsals.

Resident Patrick Nazari told the Los Angeles Times that the screams sounded like “someone is getting murdered out there.”

Los Angeles City Councilmember Adrin Nazarian’s office announced the park’s update on social media Monday evening. The statement indicated that recent coaster testing met official county sound requirements, but the park elected to add extra barriers to further reduce noise levels. Construction on those barriers is scheduled to finish by early September.

“We heard you,” Nazarian’s post read. “Universal will start installing two additional sound barriers to address noise concerns.”

open image in gallery Universal Studios Hollywood will install additional sound barriers around its newest outdoor roller coaster, Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift, following noise complaints from nearby residents ( Getty )

Universal had already incorporated sound walls, scream shields and pea gravel inside the coaster tracks to dampen sound before testing, according to a website dedicated to the ride’s considerations for its surrounding community.

Neighbors have said that the machinery itself runs quietly, but the noise became problematic once test runs began carrying passengers.

Resident Colby Jensen told KTLA that the constant shouting sounded like “a horror film going on.” Another neighbor, Leonard R. Garner Jr., told the Los Angeles Times, “I heard it, and I thought to myself, ‘There are going to be problems with this.’”

In a statement to The Independent, a Universal Studios spokesperson said that testing completed to date showed that the attraction was “operating in compliance with sound ordinance requirements.”

“Community feedback has been an important part of our testing process and in response to that feedback, we are implementing additional sound-reduction measures to further lessen sound levels in the adjacent neighborhood,” the spokesperson said. “We appreciate the community’s input and will continue to engage with our neighbors as the coaster remains in technical rehearsals ahead of its opening.”

open image in gallery Universal Studios Hollywood’s new Fast & Furious ride features rotating vehicles moving at speeds up to 72 mph ( Getty )

Universal and the Toluca Lake Homeowners Association plan to hold a community meeting to address local concerns. The park has also arranged a community hotline and installed monitoring microphones in the neighborhood, according to KTLA.

“You do hear the screaming, and I heard it late last night with the doors closed and you’re kind of like, what is that?” Toluca Lake resident John Heim told ABC 7 Los Angeles. “By the third time, you know what it is.”

Heim added that though mitigation efforts were noticeable, sound levels still varied depending on the day.

An official opening date for the ride has not yet been announced.

The Independent has contacted Universal Studios Hollywood for comment.

Paula Radcliffe has described the empty stands at the European Athletics Championships as “a shame” after the event in Birmingham came under fire for its expensive prices.

Nearly 10,000 empty seats were available on the first evening of the Championships as 13,623 people watched Great Britain’s Amy Hunt sprint her way to 100m glory at the Alexander Stadium.

Extortionate food and drinks prices have also been called out – supporters are being made to pay as much as £18.50 for a BBQ pork roll and chips, while a bottle of water costs nearly £4 from vendors in and around the stadium.

Fans were being made to pay £150 for a Category A ticket on Monday evening and while prices for those tickets dropped by £40 for Tuesday and Wednesday, they rocket back up to £150 for the final four evenings of the tournament with no discount for concessions. The cheapest ticket in Category E is £26.

open image in gallery Fans can buy a BBQ roll and chips for £18.50 (Sunny Badwal/PA)

Radcliffe – who competed for Great Britain at four consecutive Olympic Games between 1996 and 2008 – exclusively told the Press Association: “It is a shame because I think there is the willingness but I don’t know whether perhaps as a sport we need to look at the pricing and accessibility for those tickets.

“Nothing beats a stadium seeing a home victory, feeling the buzz and the hairs on your arms stand up, it’s really special.

“It’s fighting with many more different sports now, that’s the truth. We have so many different sports available to choose from, it’s about standing above the rest.

“It’s about giving the opportunity to see and experience it live in person but some people are not able to afford expensive prices.

“Something like athletics, the best experience is in the stadium or on the side of the road rather than TV.”

Attendance on Tuesday evening was seemingly higher but empty seats were still scattered across the stadium to watch the men’s 100m athletes in action.

Fans turned up to the Alexander Stadium to find there is no on-site parking and are being forced to cough up £22.50 for a park and ride service which serves as an inconvenience.

Many people have spoken out on social media while former Aston Villa striker Stan Collymore also branded the pricing “tone deaf”.

He posted on X: “Weather is amazing and the sport needs as many eyeballs as possible so kids for a quid!! £150/£100/£70 for the 3 categories at the weekend is aimed at who? Not families and kids who may want to be athletes!”

All eyes are on the championships in the UK this week after London formally submitted a bid to host the 2029 World Athletics Championships in London and the empty seats inside stadiums are not a good look.

Some prices on the concourse differ from the food vans sitting on the premises and PA understands that organisers have no control over the expensive sausage rolls outside the stadium.

Birmingham 2026 responded to criticism and said they were “delighted” with ticket sales which have “surpassed” targets and say Friday, Saturday and Sunday evening sessions are approaching sell-out.

Secretary of State for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport Lisa Nandy also defended ticket prices and says numbers will pick up as the week goes on.

She said: “Some of the ticket prices are higher but half of all the tickets here at the championships are £30 and under. Organisers have really worked to make it accessible.

“The numbers have been a bit low being the first few days. I think we will see that rise steadily and hoping for big numbers this weekend.”

A coalition including Human Rights Watch and three additional advocacy groups filed a lawsuit against the Trump administration on Tuesday, taking aim at its persistent actions against the International Criminal Court. The legal filing contends that sanctions targeting ICC prosecutors and judges impede the prosecution of individuals accused of grave international atrocities.

Submitted in the Southern District of New York, the complaint asserts that President Donald Trump's executive order issued last year, along with U.S. sanctions directed at three Palestinian rights groups and a U.N. human rights expert, represents a "blatantly illegal attack on international justice and should be struck down," a press release stated.

The court action serves as the latest effort by organizations resisting what they characterize as the Trump administration’s measures to erode international legal frameworks and disrupt global efforts targeting government impunity.

"The fact that so many leading human rights and humanitarian organizations have come together to challenge Trump’s unlawful executive order demonstrates the widespread harm it is causing across civil society groups dedicated to bringing those responsible for grave crimes to justice," said Andrew Loewenstein of Foley Hoag LLP, the lead counsel representing the plaintiffs.

Last month, Marco Rubio announced that the US was launching a ‘sweeping campaign to dismantle the threat posed by the International Criminal Court to US sovereignty’ ( AP Photo/Tierney L. Cross )

The groups assert that the financial and legal penalties against the ICC have forced them to “curtail a wide range of human rights and legal work in violation of their First and Fifth Amendment rights under the US Constitution and under the Religious Freedom Restoration Act.”

Other organizations joining the lawsuit are the American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights and the Open Society Institute.

The U.S. and Israel are not among the ICC’s member states, and neither nation recognizes the court’s authority. A White House official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity to discuss ongoing litigation, dismissed the lawsuit Tuesday, saying that the ICC’s actions have infringed on the sovereignty and national security of the U.S. and its closest ally, Israel. The State Department did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Efforts to retain the global tribunal's power come as the ICC faces enormous pressure, both internally and from its more than 120 member states. Among those sanctioned by the U.S. last year was Karim Khan, who was the ICC’s chief prosecutor until he was removed from the post last month, nearly two years after sexual misconduct allegations against him first emerged, as detailed in stories by The Associated Press.

The Trump administration had issued those sanctions against Khan and a dozen other ICC staff in retaliation for warrants the court has issued for top Israeli officials, including Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, over the war in Gaza and investigations into U.S. personnel in Afghanistan.

“The Trump administration seeks a get out of jail free card for whomever it chooses. And with this case, we say no,” Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch, said during a press conference Tuesday.

Last month, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced that the U.S. was launching a “sweeping campaign to dismantle the threat posed by the International Criminal Court to U.S. sovereignty.”

In a video message, Rubio said the U.S. would pressure member states to withdraw from the institution, sanction organizations that work with the court and ban staff from traveling to the United States. Countries that “enjoy the benefits of the U.S. security umbrella” will be called upon to reject the court’s jurisdiction over U.S. citizens, he added.

Several countries, including U.S.-allied Venezuela, announced they would withdraw from the court shortly after Rubio's statements and Khan's removal.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register or login to an existing telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football launched on August 10, 2026. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.

How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games. Last season Mark Flekken came out on top with 153 saves for Brentford, so it will be interesting to see how Caoimhin Kelleher gets on this season.



What counts as a Save?



A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

News.title: Arsenal lose second successive pre-season friendly after parading Guimaraes
News.content:
Premier League champions Arsenal continue their preparations for the new season as they take on Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup. Arsenal beat Spanish side Athletic Bilbao 3-0 in the 2025 edition, with goals from Viktor Gyokeres, Bukayo Saka and Kai Havertz sealing victory. These sides met during the 2014/15 Champions League group stages, with both games being won 2-0 by the home side.

Arsenal beat Girona 4-1 just over a week ago but fell to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night. Reflecting on that defeat, Mikel Arteta expressed his frustration at the way his side conceded the goals.

“I am disappointed with the result,” Arteta told Arsenal’s in-house media. “We are here to win football matches. We had some fantastic moments in the first half, the way we played, the way we opened them up. We have to score first, clearly, in the two chances that we had before the score.

“I am very disappointed in the manner that we conceded the first goal, the two giveaways leading to the other two goals. It is true that the finishing quality from them was exceptional, but to win a football match, you have to compete at a different level, especially in those areas of the pitch and that is the learning from today [last Wednesday].”

This is in fact Arsenal’s first game at the Emirates since being crowned Premier League champions, as they sealed the title with a game to spare, with that final match of last season being away at Crystal Palace. After today, Arsenal have two more games, including the Community Shield in a week’s time, before they kick off the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry. The likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Martin Zubimendi are still yet to return after their World Cup exploits.

Dortmund, led by Niko Kovac, finished second in the Bundesliga last season, 16 points off winners Bayern Munich. They have played four pre-season friendlies thus far, winning twice and losing twice. The likes of Karim Adeyemi, Julian Brandt and Niklas Sule have left the club this summer.

Team news to follow shortly.

Sports.title: Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma
Sports.content:
Real Madrid plot shock Martin Zubimendi transfer as Arsenal left with dilemma

Real Madrid failed with a late attempt to lure Martin Zubimendi to the Bernabeu last summer but could now make another play for the Spaniard's services this month

View 2 Images Martin Zubimendi is again being courted by Real Madrid (Image: Getty Images)

Real Madrid are said to be considering a surprise swoop for Arsenal's Martin Zubimendi - 12 months after failing to hijack the midfield maestro's move to the Premier League champions.

‌



Zubimendi was courted by a whole host of Europe's elite during his time at Real Sociedad with Liverpool going close to signing the 27-year-old back in the summer of 2024. The player had a late change of heart back then and chose to stay in Spain before moving to Arsenal during last summer's transfer window, despite late interest from Real Madrid.

‌



The playmaker featured in all 38 Premier League matches in his maiden season as a Gunner to help the club win their first league title in more than 20 years.

‌



But with Arsenal splashing out £75million on Bruno Guimaraes to further strengthen their midfield options, The Sun claim Real are ready to rekindle their interest in Zubimendi.

Myles Lewis-Skelly has made his preference clear as Man Utd and Chelsea sounded out READ MORE :

Whether Zubimendi is attainable or not is another matter with Mikel Arteta known to be a huge fan of the midfielder. It is thought, though, that Arsenal will have to sell if they are to give themselves the financial flexibility in the transfer market to 'level up' the team that almost completed the double last year after reaching the Champions League final, as per Arteta's wishes. And that could leave them with some difficult decisions to make in terms of outgoings.

It emerged on Tuesday that another highly-regarded player, Myles Lewis-Skelly, has been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United. It is currently unclear if Arsenal's London rivals will make a move for the 19-year-old Hale End graduate, though United are not expected to.

‌



Real Madrid's need for a midfielder is nothing new and they were previously believed to be the frontrunners to sign Rodri, with the Manchester City star open to a return to Spain this summer.

View 2 Images Real Madrid were favourites to sign Rodri but he now seems to be Barcelona-bound

The 30-year-old has entered the final year of his contract at The Etihad and the former Ballon d'Or winner was viewed as the ideal fit for the midfielder Jose Mourinho wants this summer.

Article continues below

But Real are now said to be behind Barcelona in the race for Rodri's services, even though their arch-rivals have seen an opening bid for the player turned down by City.

Sports.title: Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem
Sports.content:
Martin Zubimendi dilemma shows Mikel Arteta and Arsenal face new transfer problem

Martin Zubimendi is being linked with the Arsenal exit door after only one year and the signing of Bruno Guimaraes suggests the Spaniard will be shunted down the pecking order

View 4 Images Arsenal signing of Bruno Guimaraes could have a knock on affect on the squad (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

When someone of Bruno Guimaraes' calibre arrives at Arsenal, amid all the fanfare, there will be someone wondering if their time is up.

‌



The Brazilian has just moved to the Emirates for £75million after making it known that the Gunners were the club for him. This is a player who could play for any team in Europe and he will inevitably make Arsenal better.

‌



But following his arrival, that leaves one player having to go out and as part of the fallout reports have emerged that Arsenal have named their price on Martin Zubimendi. That generally only happens for players who could be on the move.

‌



You don't see any prices being quoted for Declan Rice, because he's one of Arsenal's untouchables, if they ever did make such a list. Zubimendi less so and after only a year at Arsenal the Spaniard could be set for a new role, and one he may not enjoy, if he stays.

It's a huge change for a player who, it was well documented, Mikel Arteta had eyed for several years before eventually luring him to London. This was a player who dominated England in the Euro 2024 final, making replacing Rodri look a simple task.

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

But elite clubs only go looking for players in areas where they think they can improve. You hear no noise around Arsenal landing a top class centre-half, because in William Saliba and Gabriel, they have what they need. You hear no noise around Manchester City signing a top tier No.9, because they have Erling Haaland.

‌



Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes showed that they feel they can upgrade in that position. Rice is their talisman but alongside him there's been plenty of contenders. Mikel Merino is one, albeit very versatile, Zubimendi another. Myles Lewis-Skelly may have ambitions to play in that role.

If Zubimendi is to shift from a player who was guaranteed to start to one who isn't, then perhaps the warning signs were there. This is a player who started 34 of 38 games last season - but was benched for three of the final four.

View 4 Images Martin Zubimendi increasingly found himself on the bench towards the end of the season

‌



The Spaniard's minutes were cut and he endured the embarrassment of being subbed on, and then off, by Arteta. That came in the vital win over West Ham with Zubimendi coming on in the 28th minute for the injured Ben White. But his afternoon lasted less than 40 minutes and he was hauled off in the 67th minute for Kai Havertz.

"It is never easy to do that to a player, especially someone with Martin’s quality," Arteta admitted after the game.

Weeks later and Lewis-Skelly, who had been snubbed for much of the season, was picked to play in the Champions League final against PSG. Zubimendi started on the bench, and that's where he would remain for the evening.

‌



Managers can talk all they want about the value and the importance of a player, but what really tells is whether they call upon them come crunch time. With the title in the balance and a European Cup on the line, Zubimendi found himself overlooked.

View 4 Images The Spaniard did claim the Premier League title in his first campaign with Arsenal

When Zubimendi signed from Real Sociedad the club's sporting director, Andrea Berta, claimed: "Martin was a key target for us and we all know that he is a perfect fit for our squad with the high quality he has."

‌



That fit does not look so perfect now following Arsenal's pursuit of Guimaraes. Arteta has a squad that is the envy of most of Europe, but he'll find that having so many options creates as many problems as solutions it solves.

Arsenal have effectively played with two holding midfielders and a 10, previously Martin Odegaard. The Norwegian too is a man under pressure for his spot. Going on the fact that Rice is the pillar and Guimaraes, the second most expensive player in Arsenal history, will start - where does that leave Zubimendi?

View 4 Images Mikel Arteta has some difficult decisions regarding the make-up of his midfield

‌



A possibility exists that Arsenal play with more of a flat three in midfield. But where does that leave Odegaard. Or Eberechi Eze, who played centrally last season, or Kai Havertz or eventually Max Dowman?

Arsenal were pipped on penalties by PSG last season as their European Cup dreams were ended in heartbreaking fashion. On that night in Budapest, for all their battling spirit and defensive quality, it was clear that the Gunners had levels to go in the final third to match PSG.

This summer has been about closing that gap. Guimaraes is the type of player who helps them play through the lines. Their pursuit of Vinicius Junior was well publicised.

‌



Arsenal are firmly back among Europe's elite, capping an impressive rise under Arteta's leadership, but if there's one conundrum they're yet to face during the assembly of their stunning squad, it is who to back. In recent years no major player has wanted out, but with so many top class operators now available some will inevitably end up being cannon fodder in the club's grand plan.

Zubimendi may be one of the early lessons.

Sports.title: Rodri has a huge transfer decision to make - he's outgrown Man City and MUST leave
Sports.content:
Rodri has a huge transfer decision to make - he's outgrown Man City and MUST leave

Manchester City midfielder Rodri is wanted by Spain's two biggest clubs and can pretty much take his pick with his future - his decision should be to LEAVE the Premier League

View Image Rodri has proved himself again to be the best midfielder on the planet (Image: 2026 Luciano Lima)

Rodri has the kind of choice to make most footballers can only dream about. And remaining at Manchester City should NOT be one of them.

‌



When Real Madrid and Barcelona come calling at the same time, it speaks volumes for your standing in the game. Two of the biggest clubs on the planet going head-to-head for your services. Which is how it should be, because Rodri is the best midfielder on the planet.

‌



A footballer who has outgrown his current club.

‌



Rodri has nothing left to prove or achieve in the blue half of Manchester. He has won the lot, including a Treble in 2023, having had a crucial role in elevating City to the ultimate level. And with Pep Guardiola having walked into the sunset, it feels like the time is now right for Rodri to seek a fresh challenge at the age of 30.

Ryan Reynolds delivers perfect response to US couple moving from Texas to Wrexham READ MORE :

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

The Spaniard is at his peak. He proved this in the summer, leading Spain to World Cup glory.

Having now won the ultimate prize, to sit alongside the Euros triumph of 2024, Ballon d'Or accolade and countless club trophies, there might be little left for Rodri to aim for.

‌



But someone like him should be desperate to add more layers to his legacy. And the place to do this should either be in Barcelona or Madrid.

The Nou Camp and Bernabeu are two genuine cathedrals of football. Fitting stages for the incredible talents Rodri has.

Turning down Real in favour of Barca would not be everyone's choice. When it comes to history, tradition and standing in the game, no-one quite compares to the 15-time Champions League winners. A club the great Guardiola once labelled the "kings of Europe".

‌



But joining Barca, like what Rodri is expected to do in the coming days, would be quite the second prize. The reigning Spanish champions remain a monster of a club.

One the likes of City will never be able to draw comparisons with. One with millions of supporters around the globe. One which has winning the biggest club prizes embedded in its DNA.

Rodri owes City nothing.

‌



He cost them £62.6m from Atletico Madrid, but went on to become a priceless addition to the team's progress. So if and when Rodri decides to say goodbye to the Etihad, supporters should bid him a fond farewell and give him their blessing.

While City bosses should give fans a lasting reminder of how much he contributed. By giving the bloke a statue outside the stadium.

Sports.title: Man Utd 'ready to trigger release clause' and forced to act quick after £20m agreement
Sports.content:
Man Utd 'ready to trigger release clause' and forced to act quick after £20m agreement

Manchester United continue to be linked with a host of names, even though they have added six new faces to Michael Carrick's squad this summer

View 2 Images Michael Carrick could be getting a new left back before the season gets underway (Image: (Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images))

Manchester United are ready to trigger Jorge Salinas’ release clause - but face competition from Atletico Madrid for his signature. Salinas came through the ranks at Real Racing Club de Santander and went on to make his first-team debut back in 2024.

‌



The left-back has since impressed in Spain, and, as a result, has been linked with a move away. As well as Atletico and United, Salinas has also been linked with a move to Barcelona.

‌



However, according to Spanish publication Sport, Barca have no intention of paying Salinas’ €16m (£13.6m) release clause. United, though, are ready to trigger it to snap up the 19-year-old this summer.

‌



But in a twist, the report also claims that Atletico are waiting for Matteo Ruggeri to complete a move to Aston Villa before making a move for Salinas. It is claimed that Villa have agreed a €18m plus €6m bonuses (£20m) deal with Los Rojiblancos for Ruggeri, meaning United may have to act quickly.

Despite the continued speculation around Salinas’ future, Racing boss Jose Alberto Lopez claimed earlier this week that the defender, along with Gustavo Puerta, don’t want to leave the club this summer. He said: "Their professionalism doesn't surprise me.

What Marcus Rashford really thinks about staying at Manchester United this season READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR MAN UNITED FB PAGE! Latest news and analysis via the MEN’s Manchester United Facebook page

‌



“What surprises me is that people are constantly talking about the departure of two of our players [Salinas and Puerta], when they have contracts and are our players."

Before he added: "They're very important to us. I don't want them to leave. And they show every day that they don't either.

“But we know how this world works and there are release clauses. If a team comes along and pays the clause, they cease to be our players."

‌



View 2 Images Jorge Salinas is a key target with United said to be ready to meet his release clause

Speaking last week, Racing sporting director Chema Aragon made similar comments, but he did admit that his club would be powerless if a 'giant' such as United and Barca came in with a significant bid for Salinas.

"There's little you can do if a giant appears," Aragan said. "We value the assets we have, we consider them important.

‌



“For the club, at this time, there is no other option than to try to strengthen the team and not weaken it by losing stars. The reality is that the club that wants him has to come along with an offer."

United are in the market for a left back and are considering alternatives for Lewis Hall, who Newcastle do not want to sell. Salinas has already represented Spain's under-19 side nine times and registered seven assists from 34 matches last season as Racing were promoted back to La Liga.

Sports.title: Paul Scholes begs Man Utd to sign £30m 'absolute idiot' and admits 'you might laugh'
Sports.content:
Paul Scholes begs Man Utd to sign £30m 'absolute idiot' and admits 'you might laugh'

Cristian Romero is set to leave Tottenham this summer and Manchester United legend Paul Scholes has urged his former club to hijack the transfer

View 2 Images Paul Scholes is a fan of Cristian Romero (Image: PA)

Paul Scholes believes Manchester United should try to hijack a move for Cristian Romero, whom he described as an 'absolute idiot.' The Argentine, appointed captain only last year after signing a four‑year deal, is expected to leave Tottenham this summer, with Atletico Madrid currently in negotiations over his transfer.

‌



Fabrizio Romano reports that the deal between Spurs and Atletico is edging closer, though clubs are still a few million apart on the guaranteed fee and have yet to finalise the bonus structure. Atletico remain determined and are preparing a new offer.

‌



Inter Milan, Barcelona and Arsenal have also shown interest, but a sale to Spurs' north London rivals appears highly unlikely. Despite Romero favouring Atleti, Scholes believes United should attempt a late hijack, arguing that adding a top‑level centre‑back alongside Lisandro Martinez and Harry Maguire would be crucial as they prepare for a demanding season across all competitions.

‌



Audacious Marcus Rashford swap deal proposed with Arsenal star joining Man Utd READ MORE :

Man Utd preparing for four transfer exits as Michael Carrick green lights departures READ MORE :

"This is one you might laugh at," Scholes said on The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast. "[United should sign] Cristian Romero from Tottenham. I know he's a nutter. I know he's got disciplinary issues.

"But I just think he can be a very good centre-half and I think someone like Michael [Carrick] could really calm him down. And you're talking 30 or 40 million quid. This is a fella who's played centre half and won the World Cup. Now, like I said, I know he's got issues, disciplinary issues."

Scholes added: "There's a bit of something about him. He's won the Europa League with Spurs, he's won a World Cup, two Copa Americas. There's definitely something about him....and he's cheap, £30-40million.

‌



"I think centre-half is probably the biggest [area that needs addressing]. You need to have centre-halves that are reliable for the Premier League. You'd like to have them [fit enough to play] in most games.

View 2 Images Paul Scholes would like to see Romero at Man United

"Harry Maguire not so much, but Martinez picks up a lot of injuries. They've got the young lad Ayden Heaven, who I think is a really bright prospect, but he's still going to make mistakes. He's young. Centre-half is a position they need to address if they are going to be challenging towards the top end [of the league]."

‌



Romero previously came close to leaving Spurs, most notably after Ange Postecoglou's departure. Roberto De Zerbi has since made it clear that he would respect Romero's wish to move on from north London.

"At the beginning of my time, in April, I had, I don't know, one million individual meetings!" he said. "And [the players] told me what was their idea. I said: 'Yes, help me to stay up, and then I help you to leave'. If you don't help me to stay up, you stay underwater with me!"

"But Romero with me was unbelievable. Top. In his behaviour, his respect, he suffered when he did not play the last game. It is not true that he wanted to leave for Argentina to prepare for their World Cup. It's not true."

‌



FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

De Zerbi added: "After the semi-final [against England] we text a message, but I never called him to convince him to stay. I respected what he told me. Like for Vicario, like for every player. Romero as a player is one of the best centre-backs in the world, but at the end I said I want to respect the will of the players."

United have already added three new faces to Michael Carrick's squad - Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans and Karl Darlow. With the window running until 1 September, there's still time for another defensive signing, and Bologna centre‑back Jhon Lucumi is one of the names in the frame.

Article continues below

The Colombia international, who featured at the World Cup, is said to be keen on joining a 'big club' this summer. Bologna want £21.4m (€25m) plus £2.6m (€3m) in bonuses, and United are considering whether to match the asking price.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer

Arsenal could have Newcastle United to thank for a summer transfer boost days after raiding St James' Park to sign Bruno Guimaraes

View 2 Images Arsenal signed Bruno Guimaraes from Newcastle United for £75m but could recoup millions (Image: (Photo by David Price/Arsenal FC via Getty Images))

Arsenal could be set to recoup some of the £75m transfer fee they paid for Bruno Guimaraes just days later, thanks to a shrewd transfer clause included as part of Joe Willock's switch to Newcastle United. The Gunners negotiated a sell-on clause with the Magpies when Willock moved to St. James' Park back in 2021.

‌



The 26-year-old left the Emirates Stadium in a deal valued at £25million after an impressive loan spell with the Magpies, but his five-year stay in the North East may be coming to an end. Willock is now believed to be close to a £17.4m move to Turkish Super Lig outfit Besiktas, with Newcastle having turned down a £10m bid earlier this summer.

‌



Our sister title ChronicleLive reports Willock's representatives have travelled to Turkey to negotiate a move with Besiktas, reportedly reaching agreement on personal terms. The former Arsenal midfielder is entering the final 12 months of his contract at St. James' Park and Newcastle are keen to recoup a fee.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

That's positive news for the Gunners, who secured a sell-on clause rumoured to be around 20 per cent, though the precise percentage remains undisclosed. Arsenal spent £75m to take Guimaraes to north London and could bank millions from Willock's prospective move, recouping some of the money paid for the Brazilian.

Gunners fans got a first glimpse of the new midfield addition ahead of the Emirates Cup clash with Borussia Dortmund at the weekend. As for his former Magpies teammate, Willock has featured 168 times for Newcastle, netting 11 goals since his departure from the Gunners.

‌



He broke into the Arsenal first team in 2017 and memorably scored on his Premier League debut against Newcastle in April 2018. Willock racked up 78 appearances and registered 11 goals during four campaigns at the club.

View 2 Images Willock found a new home in the north east (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

The clause now ensures Mikel Arteta's side will profit financially. Arsenal are looking to bolster their squad ahead of their Premier League title defence, having already brought in Christos Tzolis, Piero Hincapie, Illan Meslier and Guimaraes.

‌



The additional funds will provide a welcome boost in their bid to secure further signings this summer, with the Gunners actively seeking a new left-winger.

Arsenal had been linked with moves for Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, however Chelsea swooped in to snap up the England international, while Real Madrid tied down the Brazilian star to fresh terms.

Sports.title: SunRisers beat Super Giants to reach Hundred eliminator
Sports.content:
Reigning champions SunRisers Leeds snatched a spot in the women's Hundred eliminator by beating Manchester Super Giants by 41 runs in a winner-takes-all game at Old Trafford.

In a shoot-out for the final place in the top three, Annabel Sutherland's unbeaten 62 off 36 balls helped Leeds leapfrog their opponents and set up an eliminator clash against Southern Brave.

The Australian all-rounder hit nine boundaries, including three sixes, as the visitors posted 166-4 after being put in to bat.

Visiting spinner Jess Jonassen took 3-21, while Deepti Sharma and Sutherland claimed two wickets apiece, as Manchester were restricted to 125-8 in reply and exited the competition after slipping to fourth place in the standings.

Second-placed Leeds will continue their title defence against Southern Brave on Friday at The Oval, with table-topping Trent Rockets awaiting the winner in Sunday's final at Lord's.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player UNBELIEVABLE athletic fielding from SunRisers' Phoebe Litchfield to prevent a six

Sutherland, the Match Hero, said: "It's the beauty of being an all-rounder, you're in the game all the time, and I love competing, especially in a match we were calling a final. We had to win and it was nice to do a job for the team."

Phoebe Litchfield made her intentions clear after SunRisers were asked to bat, the Aussie opener racing to 27 from 12 deliveries to leapfrog Sophia Dunkley at the top of the competition's run-scoring chart.

An electrifying innings was brought to a halt after Litchfield miscued a drag down from Mady Villiers but Bryony Smith (17 off 16) and Lauren Winfield-Hill (20 off 15) kept the scoreboard ticking.

Smith holed out to Villiers off Kathryn Bryce and Winfield-Hill was run out after a mix-up to leave the score 83-3 before Sutherland took charge, aided by a sparky cameo from Dani Gibson (24 off 13).

When Gibson fell to Villiers with 12 balls remaining, SunRisers were handily placed on 119-4, and Sutherland propelled the visitors to 166-4 - the highest score in the women's competition at Emirates Old Trafford - carting the unfortunate Ryana MacDonald-Gay for three consecutive sixes to round off the innings.

The Super Giants made a strong start in reply before Jonassen claimed the key scalp of Smriti Mandhana for 28, yorking the Indian with a cleverly-flighted delivery.

Grave Scrivens struck six fours in her 24-ball 31 before being stumped by Winfield-Hill off the irrepressible Sutherland (2-17), and Richa Ghosh departed two deliveries later after holing out to give Jonassen her second.

Bryce retired out after making 15 from 14 and even the great Meg Lanning (10 off 15) could not find any momentum, bowled by Jonassen as the Super Giants laboured to 125-8.

After a slow start to the tournament, the SunRisers will take a four-match winning streak into Friday's showdown at The Oval.

Sports.title: Levy goes up against Spurs owners to buy London's NBA Europe team
Sports.content:
Former Tottenham chairman Daniel Levy is vying with a consortium including current Spurs' owners, the Lewis family, to buy NBA Europe's London-based team.

Sky News has revealed that the Lewises are part of a consortium, led by the Checketts family, which has submitted an offer as part of the ongoing auction.

The Checketts have owned or invested in professional sports franchises including Major League Soccer team Real Salt Lake and the NHL's St Louis Blues.

The third leg of the consortium is the Eccles family, who own shares in Burnley FC and Spanish side Espanyol along with the Checketts.

Sky News has previously reported Levy's involvement in a consortium including Liberty Global and MSP Sports Capital, a former backer of McLaren Racing, which is also among the contenders for the NBA London team.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Kaveh Solhekol examines where Daniel Levy was 'pushed' out of his role as Spurs chairman

London has rapidly become most highly prized of the 12 new NBA Europe outfits, with other teams based in cities such as Berlin, Manchester, Milan, Munich, Paris and Rome.

The NBA wants to generate billions of dollars by selling the rights to the teams, with the first transactions expected in the coming weeks.

Wealthy US families and investors are increasingly buying stakes in sports teams in the UK, especially in football.

Levy left his role as Spurs executive chairman in September 2025 after nearly 25 years in the job.

While the official communication from Spurs and Levy was that he had "stepped down" from the role, it was widely understood that the decision was taken out of his hands.

Sports.title: Floodlights to be on throughout Hundred matches for solar eclipse
Sports.content:
Floodlights will be turned on throughout games in The Hundred on Wednesday due to the solar eclipse.

Up to 90 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon during the eclipse, which will occur between 6.17pm and 8.06pm, peaking shortly after 7pm.

It will be the first partial solar eclipse for 27 years and will be visible across Europe, with some places experiencing a total eclipse, where the sun, moon and earth all line up in space.

The light will dim, the temperature will drop and the wind may change direction as the sun disappears behind the moon. After a few minutes the sun will reappear and daylight will return.

There are four games in The Hundred taking place on Wednesday, all of them live on Sky Sports.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Take a look at the best moments from this year's Hundred.

Welsh Fire women face London Spirit women at 11.30am in Cardiff, followed by the men's game at 3pm. Birmingham Phoenix women host MI London at Edgbaston from 3pm before the men's teams play each other at 6.30pm.

In anticipation for the solar eclipse, organisers will keep floodlights on throughout all four matches and additional messaging will be issued to fans.

Experts have warned that only special solar eclipse glasses that are certified for the safest eye protection should be used to view the eclipse.

Floodlights will be on 'plenty early' at Kempton

Kempton is all set to stage racing on Wednesday during the solar eclipse.

While the twilight meeting at Ffos Las will begin and end earlier than originally scheduled to ensure all six races take place in daylight, there are no such issues at Kempton due to the floodlights that are in place at the Sunbury circuit.

Image: The floodlights will also be turned on at Kempton race course

The eclipse is expected to occur between 7.02pm and 7.16pm and Kempton has races scheduled to take place at 7pm and 7.30pm.

Kempton's clerk of the course Barney Clifford said: "The last one was nearly 30 years ago so I wasn't quite at Kempton then. I remember it but there were no floodlights in those days!

"I'm going to put the floodlights on early doors. I know they have predicted a time for it but you don't quite know how much of the sun is going to be covered and for what race so we'll have the lights on plenty early enough."

Sports.title: Inter Milan in talks over Spurs and England defender Spence
Sports.content:
Tottenham are in talks with Inter Milan over the sale of Djed Spence.

Inter believe a total package of £30m could be enough to get a deal done and Spurs are understood to be willing to sell if they receive an acceptable offer.

Spence's opportunities could be limited at Spurs this season with Destiny Udogie and Andy Robertson also competing for the left-back position and the ever-present Pedro Porro the clear first choice on the right.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player After Spence's brilliant cameo off the bench against Norway, England fans Ben Cipolla and Dan Lucas came up with a new song for the full-back titled 'Total Eclipse of Djed Spence'

Inter want to bring in a new player who can operate as a wing-back.

Spence has been high on their list all summer and Inter are now turning their attention to the Spurs man after struggling to strike a deal for Al Ittihad's Moussa Diaby.

De Zerbi: Spurs aren't done in the transfer window

Roberto de Zerbi maintains Tottenham are "not finished yet" in the transfer market as they look to build a competitive Premier League squad again.

Having only avoided relegation on the final day of last season, Spurs have spent already spent around £237m - with the club's transfer record broken twice in deals for Mateus Fernandes and Sandro Tonali.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Tottenham Hotspur head coach Roberto De Zerbi tells the Men in Blazers Network that he expects to make more signings this summer (Pictures: Men in Blazers Network)

Dutch defender Jan Paul van Hecke also arrived from Brighton for £52m, while Martin Dubravka, Robertson and Marcos Senesi signed on as free agents.

With Micky van de Ven having also committed his long-term future to the club, there is genuine hope Spurs will soon be challenging at the other end of the table.

"In the transfer market, we have not finished yet [with] the players who will arrive," De Zerbi said, speaking to the Men in Blazers Network.

"We are looking forward to start another season with, I don't know [different] ambitions, but with different results."

De Zerbi continued: "The club has been great because they closed [deals for] very, very important players. I think we have not finished yet.

"Okay, we spent money, but the other clubs made the same or more in the past. To compete in the Premier League, you need first [the] level of the players.

"The ambition of the owner of the club, of the board, of the people who decide behind me are very important and very high, so we have to find the condition to build a strong team, a stronger team than the last seasons, to compete again for the top of the table."

Sports.title: Unbeaten star Bow Echo in shock retirement after setback
Sports.content:
Bow Echo has been retired from racing after the shock news that George Boughey's unbeaten star has suffered a setback in training.

Having won the 2000 Guineas, the St James's Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot and the Sussex Stakes this season, Bow Echo was being lined up for Sunday's Prix Jacques le Marois.

Announcing the surprise news on his X account, Boughey said: "It is with great disappointment that we have to announce that Bow Echo has had a setback and will be retired from racing.

"It has been the honour of a lifetime to train a horse like Bow Echo. He has given us some extraordinary days and taken everyone involved on a journey we will never forget.

"To retire unbeaten, having won the 2000 Guineas, St James's Palace Stakes and Sussex Stakes says everything about what an exceptional racehorse he has been.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Bow Echo and Gstaad served up a thriller in the St James's Palace Stakes on day one of Royal Ascot

"Bow Echo's remarkable story began with his owner-breeder, the late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and it is a great sadness that he was not here to see what a lifetime of breeding was able to produce.

"Bow Echo's unbelievable constitution and extraordinary ability have set him apart. We will all miss seeing him at home and on the racecourse but we are incredibly excited for his next chapter and in time, to see a new generation of his progeny on the racecourse."

Sports.title: Chelsea make enquiry for Arsenal's Lewis-Skelly
Sports.content:
Chelsea have made a new enquiry about signing Arsenal's Myles Lewis-Skelly.

The Blues have a long-term interest in the midfielder and have made another check on his availability following Arsenal's signing of Bruno Guimaraes.

However, Arsenal do not want to sell Lewis-Skelly to a local rival and a team they may have to compete with for the top places this season. Chelsea were linked with Lewis-Skelly in January.
