Sports.title: Hearn: Devin Haney Wants Purse Without Promotional Risk
Sports.content:
“The reality is a lot of these fighters have this sort of grand illusion that they really can run their own promotional company and take over,” Hearn told the Punch Podcast. “They love to have a promotional company, and they love their logo on the ring mat and on the poster, but I’ve worked with these guys before, Devin Haney included, and when it comes down to it, they don’t really want to take any responsibility or financial risk in a show.”

Hearn gave an example involving Haney, claiming he offered a true co-promotional partnership that was quickly turned down.

“I’ve said to Devin before, you know, if you want, we’ll go 50/50 on the show. Oh, no, no, no. I said, but if it don’t work, are you going to pay half? No. Just what’s my purse?”

A true 50-50 arrangement would require sharing the financial downside if an event failed to generate enough revenue.

“You want David Diamante to go, ‘In association with Devin Haney Promotions,’” Hearn continued.

While Haney now enjoys greater control over his career decisions, Hearn maintains that independent fighters still depend on established promoters to execute major events. He pointed to Rolando Romero’s fight against Teofimo Lopez as a PBC operation, despite the fighters maintaining their own business banners.

“These guys don’t have the infrastructure and the ability to run high-level operations and shows,” Hearn said.

While maintaining a promotional entity gives Haney leverage at the negotiating table, Hearn’s point remains simple: putting your logo on a poster is vastly different from putting your own money on the line.

Sports.title: Guido Vianello Added To Thin Itauma-Hrgovic PPV
Sports.content:
The 14-3-1 contender is coming off a fifth-round knockout of Alexis Barriere last October. His recent opposition includes Richard Torrez Jr., Arslanbek Makhmudov and Efe Ajagba.

An eighth-round stoppage of Makhmudov in August 2024 is the best result on his record, coming four months after a close split decision loss to Ajagba. Torrez later defeated him by unanimous decision last April.

That experience gives the PPV another recognizable heavyweight on a card built around an intriguing but still unproven 21-year-old headliner.

Itauma is taking a major step up against 34-year-old Hrgovic for the vacant IBF heavyweight title. Hrgovic remains one of the division’s established contenders, but the punishment he has absorbed in recent fights has begun to show. Itauma is being given the opportunity to capitalize against a warhorse who may no longer be at his best.

Sam Noakes against 38-year-old former WBO lightweight champion Denys Berinchyk is the other recognizable supporting fight. Cruiserweight prospect Aloys Youmbi faces 40-year-old Mike Perez, while Constantin Ursu meets Ben Vaughan for the British and Commonwealth welterweight titles.

Beyond those bouts, the card relies largely on prospects and domestic-level fighters.

David Adeleye had previously been linked with Vianello before leaving Queensberry Promotions. With Vianello now confirmed for August 29, the quality of the opponent Queensberry finds for him becomes important on a PPV card that needs another meaningful fight.

Sports.title: Liam Paro Insists He Wants Devin Haney Fight, Hears Nothing
Sports.content:
“Haney is ducking me,” Paro told Fox Sports Australia. “I’ve said I’m good to fight by the end of October, and we ain’t heard a thing.”

Paro also rejected the idea that his financial demands caused negotiations to stall.

“I’ll fight him next, no worries. You know I’ll fight anyone. And I’ve proved that my whole career. I’ll fight him in his backyard or mine.”

The former IBF champion may have more to offer Haney commercially than Catterall. Paro brings name recognition and interest from the Australian market. Despite his loss to Richardson Hitchins, he remains a rugged southpaw with enough power and physical strength to make Haney work.

Catterall involves a different type of difficulty. He is a defensive southpaw who moves, potshots, pulls away when opponents close distance, and frequently ties up. That could produce a difficult tactical contest for Haney without necessarily generating the same financial upside as facing Paro.

Catterall’s willingness to step in still gives Haney an important bargaining chip. His manager, Sam Jones, says they have accepted the proposed date and location while accusing Paro of wanting too much money.

Haney also received some unwelcome news from Ryan Garcia this week. Garcia placed Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero, and Shakur Stevenson among the opponents he wants after facing Conor Benn on September 12.

“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen,” Ryan told The Ring about facing Haney again. “They have to sit with that loss.”

That leaves Haney needing someone to fight. Paro may think the silence means Haney is avoiding him, but it may simply be Team Haney waiting to see which welterweight gives them the better deal.

Sports.title: Moses Itauma Talks Like Heavyweight’s Old Guard At 21
Sports.content:
“I like Leo Atang. He’s very decent, and he’s a nice kid as well,” Itauma told DAZN News. “I like Adam Olayinan, the guy who’s just signed with Queensberry. I watched his fight the other day, and that was very good as well. “Obviously that Teremoana, he looks decent. They’re probably the ones I’m looking at for the young guns coming up. They all look decent.”

Teremoana is about to turn 29, competed in the Olympics, and trails Itauma by only three professional bouts. Calling him one of the “young guns coming up” seems odd coming from a fighter eight years his junior.

The difference is that Itauma has been pushed much faster and surrounded by considerably more hype. Wins over Dillian Whyte, Demsey McKean, Jermaine Franklin, and Mariusz Wach have helped move him up the heavyweight rankings and create the impression that he has already graduated beyond prospect status.

Those names look better on a record than the opponents the Australian Olympian has faced, but Teremoana hasn’t been given the same type of matchmaking. He has the size and punching power to potentially run through that same tier of fighters.

Itauma gets his opportunity to show how good he really is when he faces Filip Hrgovic on August 29. Hrgovic is a significant step up from the opposition Itauma has been beating and should give a better indication of where he belongs in the division.

Until then, it’s a bit early for a 21-year-old with only three more professional fights than Teremoana to talk like an established heavyweight watching the up-and-comers work their way toward him.

Sports.title: Jerry Quarry Destroys Earnie Shavers in 141 Seconds
Sports.content:
Both fighters were 28. Quarry weighed 202 pounds, eight lighter than Shavers.

The buildup had almost guaranteed violence. Quarry predicted three rounds and believed he could finish Shavers in one if his opponent came after him. Don King, then part of Shavers’ management team, called it their easiest fight. Madison Square Garden matchmaker Teddy Brenner went further, predicting the shortest 12-round fight in history. He wasn’t far off.

Trainer Gil Clancy wanted Quarry to box, but Quarry abandoned that idea almost immediately. Instead of giving Shavers room to unleash his power, he attacked him.

Quarry drove Shavers toward the ropes and unloaded lefts and rights to the head. Shavers managed to move away, but Quarry followed him across the ring and dropped him with a left-right combination.

Shavers got back up, only to find Quarry waiting for him. Quarry poured on punches as Shavers struggled to defend himself. His eyes looked unfocused, and he was taking clean shots without answering effectively. Referee Arthur Mercante had seen enough and stopped the fight at 2:21 of the opening round. There would be no need for judges Jack Gordon and Bill Recht.

The result was stunning because Quarry had beaten the knockout artist by fighting him at his own game. George Foreman, Joe Frazier, and Muhammad Ali were among the prominent names at ringside. Foreman reportedly expressed surprise that Quarry had chosen to trade with Shavers and came away impressed by his aggression.

Ali and Frazier had another reason to be at the Garden. Their January 28, 1974 rematch was already set for the same arena and was promoted during the Quarry-Shavers telecast. Frazier discussed getting his weight down and preparing for Ali before the main event, while viewers were urged to buy tickets for their second fight.

Their rematch also strengthened Quarry’s position in the heavyweight picture. With Ali and Frazier committed to fighting each other, the broadcast team noted that neither man would likely be available for Foreman until around June. Quarry’s destruction of Shavers suddenly made him an obvious candidate to challenge the champion before then.

Quarry paid a physical price despite the short night. He injured his left wrist after landing a hook high on Shavers’ head, with reports raising concern over a possible fracture.

Shavers later admitted that the first heavy blows had left him unable to recover. He regretted rising so quickly after the knockdown, believing that taking more of the count might have given him enough time to survive the remaining seconds of the round.

Nearly 15,000 spectators had come expecting to see what happened when Shavers’ frightening power collided with Quarry’s durability and experience. They barely had time to settle into their seats.

The official attendance was 14,962, producing a gate of $201,564. Quarry was guaranteed $40,000 against 30 percent of the gate, while Shavers received $30,000 against 27½ percent.

The victory strengthened Quarry’s position near the top of a stacked division ruled by Foreman, but the championship opportunity never followed. Quarry instead met Frazier again the following year and was stopped in five rounds.

Shavers rebuilt his career and eventually challenged both Ali and Larry Holmes for the heavyweight championship.

Neither man’s later career changed what happened that December night. Shavers arrived with the reputation as a devastating slugger, but Quarry never gave him enough time to use it.

For 141 seconds, Quarry simply beat him to the punch.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia Wants Haney To Stew In Loss
Sports.content:
“I’m not in a rush to make that fight happen. They have to sit with that loss,” Ryan told The Ring. “Why do I have to beg for it? I’m here. I’m about to beat up Conor Benn. I want Teofimo Lopez, Rolando Romero and Shakur Stevenson. I have a lot of options. I’m not really worried about Haney now. If it happens, it happens.”

What happened in April 2024 remains the source of the hostility. Garcia dropped Haney three times and won a majority decision before the victory was changed to a no-contest following his positive test for ostarine.

Devin and Bill Haney have repeatedly brought up the failed test since then, refusing to treat the original outcome as a legitimate defeat. Drug testing has also been a recurring subject whenever another fight with Garcia has been discussed.

Ryan’s refusal to rush into a rematch sounds personal. He has the WBC welterweight title, a September fight with Benn, and several lucrative opponents he can pursue without giving Haney an opportunity to settle the score.

“All these guys obviously have to come to me,” Ryan said. “I’m definitely the lottery fight. If you want to be a huge name, I’m the guy to do it [against]. You have to get through me.”

That is the position Garcia believes he occupies. After two years of hearing why his performance against Haney shouldn’t count, he doesn’t seem interested in helping Team Haney put it behind them.

They can sit with it.

Sports.title: Archie Moore Rallies To Stop Harold Johnson In 14
Sports.content:
Moore weighed 173 pounds to Johnson’s 172½.

Working behind his jab, movement and counterpunching, Johnson frustrated Moore through much of the early and middle rounds. His advantage grew in the 10th when a right hand behind the ear dropped the champion.

Moore rose quickly, but referee Ruby Goldstein continued counting, overlooking that the automatic eight-count had been waived for the championship fight. Moore recovered and continued pursuing Johnson.

The challenger remained in front as the fight moved into the late rounds. Two officials had Johnson leading after 13, putting Moore in danger of losing his championship on the scorecards.

Then Moore changed the fight. He hurt Johnson late in the 13th and attacked immediately when the 14th began. A barrage of rights and lefts drove Johnson into his own corner before sending him to the canvas.

Johnson regained his feet, but he was badly hurt. Moore followed him along the ropes and continued punching until Goldstein stopped the fight at 56 seconds of the 14th round.

The comeback preserved Moore’s championship and extended his winning streak to 19 fights. Johnson had come within two rounds of taking the title from a rival he had first fought in 1949.

Moore soon resumed his pursuit of heavyweight champion Rocky Marciano. He received the opportunity the following year, dropping Marciano before being stopped in the ninth round.

Johnson never received the sixth Moore fight he wanted. Years later, he became light heavyweight champion himself.

Their August 1954 battle closed a five-fight rivalry with its most dramatic ending. Johnson had the lead, but the Old Mongoose found the punches he needed before time ran out.

Sports.title: Eddie Hearn Escalates Fury-Joshua Fight Over MSG
Sports.content:
“We signed for this fight in the UK,” Hearn said to Fighthype. “We are desperate to deliver this fight for UK fans. However, everybody else wants the fight in America: Turki Alalshikh, Netflix. I can’t speak on behalf of Tyson Fury; I don’t see him kicking up a fuss. Madison Square Garden. So, they’re telling us this is the place it’s going to do the biggest numbers, this is the place it’ll be the biggest fight.”

Hearn has made his preference for Britain clear for weeks. What changes the discussion is how far he now sounds prepared to push the disagreement.

“I disagree. But at the end we’ll fight, and we’ll fight, and we’ll fight to a point where they’ve breached the contract by doing it in America, or we come to an agreement.”

That is strong language considering Hearn’s business relationship with Alalshikh and the number of major events Matchroom has staged with his involvement.

Hearn also admits the people on the other side of the venue dispute are key allies, making his willingness to discuss a potential breach of agreement more surprising.

His stated reason is loyalty to British boxing fans. But if Madison Square Garden really produces the bigger commercial event, Hearn’s resistance becomes harder to explain purely as a business decision.

There is also no indication that Fury shares Hearn’s resistance to New York. Hearn concedes he doesn’t see Fury “kicking up a fuss” about Madison Square Garden, potentially leaving Matchroom as the strongest opposition to the proposed move.

The dispute has therefore moved beyond a simple choice between Britain and New York. Hearn is now openly discussing how far Matchroom will go to enforce the agreement it signed.

Ghana News.title: ECG announces power outages in Central, Eastern and Western Regions on Thursday
Ghana News.content:
The Electricity Company of Ghana (ECG) has announced planned maintenance works in parts of the Central, Eastern and Western Regions on Thursday, August 13.

According to a statement issued on Tuesday, August 11, the exercise is aimed at improving service delivery and will result in temporary power outages in several communities during the maintenance period.

ECG said the affected customers should expect interruptions at different times depending on their location, with the outages scheduled to last between four and seven hours.

Central Region

In the Central Region, the planned maintenance works are scheduled to take place from 9:00am to 4:00pm on Thursday.

The affected areas include American Town, New Market, Colomba, Akweley, Ofaako, Papaase, Jei Krodua, Adawukwa and Bawjiase township, as well as surrounding communities.

Eastern Region

Two separate sets of communities in the Eastern Region will also be affected by the exercise.

The first group is scheduled to experience an outage from 9:00am to 1:00pm.

The affected areas are Saarfi, Ahantang, Ampayoo, Ataaso, Owusukrom, Apradang, Yawkorkor, Akroma Gold and Oworobrs, Insuta Everyday, Adensua Mission, Isaac Hotel, Abenase, Bandoh, Abusco, Akutuase and Starting Point.

For another group of communities in the Eastern Region, the planned interruption will run from 9:00am to 2:00pm.

These areas include Amanase, Mankrong, Asuboi, Kyekyewere and Ayeeh Apeatu.

Western Region

In the Western Region, ECG has scheduled the maintenance exercise from 9:00am to 3:00pm.

The affected communities are Amobaka, Diaso, Modaso, Ankwaso Juabo, Wassa Ayiem, Sraha, Agona Port, Ntom, New Obuasi, Nyinawusu, Some Asamang, Akwaboso, Subin and Ameyaw, together with surrounding areas.

ECG explains maintenance exercise

ECG said the planned interruptions form part of its efforts to carry out maintenance works aimed at improving the reliability and quality of electricity supply.

Region Time Duration Central 9:00am–4:00pm 7 hours Eastern – Group 1 9:00am–1:00pm 4 hours Eastern – Group 2 9:00am–2:00pm 5 hours Western 9:00am–3:00pm 6 hours

Ghana News.title: God does not take campaign instructions
Ghana News.content:
Rev Owusu Bempah

There is a dangerous difference between faith and arrogance, between prophecy and political theatre, and between spiritual conviction and the reckless assumption that one has been handed the keys to another man's destiny.

The statement attributed to Prophet Owusu Bempah crosses that line spectacularly.

“As long as I am alive, Bawumia will never become president.”

Really?

Since when did the lifespan of one mortal determine the political destiny of another? Since when did Ghana's electoral future become conditional upon whether a particular preacher is breathing?

No human being knows tomorrow with scientific certainty. No pastor knows it. No politician knows it. No professor knows it. No pollster knows it. Even the world's most sophisticated forecasting systems deal in probabilities, not certainties.

Elections are determined by millions of individual decisions, changing economic conditions, candidates, campaigns, alliances, events and circumstances that have not yet occurred.

Then there is destiny, for those who believe in it.

If destiny exists, surely its defining characteristic is that it is beyond the command of ordinary men. A person may predict it. He may pray about it. He may even believe he has received a revelation concerning it. But to boast that “as long as I am alive” another human being cannot attain a particular position sounds less like submission to divine authority and more like an extraordinary declaration of personal power.

And then comes the threat to “curse” people who vote differently.

That is where the whole performance descends from pomposity into absurdity.

A democracy cannot be held hostage by supernatural intimidation. The ballot belongs to the citizen. A Ghanaian must be free to vote for Bawumia, against Bawumia, or for anybody else without fearing the alleged spiritual artillery of a preacher.

If a prophecy is genuinely divine, it requires neither threats nor curses to make it happen.

History is littered with confident men who announced impossibilities shortly before those impossibilities happened. Human beings are notoriously poor custodians of tomorrow. That is precisely why humility remains one of wisdom's greatest virtues.

You may dislike Bawumia. Campaign against him. Criticise his record. Challenge his ideas. Defeat him at the ballot box.

But declaring yourself the human barricade standing between another man and his destiny is not power.

It is hot air dressed in religious authority.

Tomorrow has embarrassed bigger men.

And 2028 will arrive whether anyone curses it or not.

Ghana News.title: Government moves to address rising accommodation costs at KNUST
Ghana News.content:
The Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment, George Opare-Addo, says he will petition the Ministry of Education and other relevant authorities over the rising cost of student accommodation, particularly at the Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST).

This follows a demonstration by some KNUST students at the university’s Great Hall, where they used placards to draw attention to the increasing cost of hostel and residential accommodation.

Speaking at the launch of the National Youth Conference in Kumasi on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, Mr Opare-Addo said the government would engage the relevant authorities and hostel operators to find solutions to the concerns raised by students.

He said the government would petition the Education Ministry and other institutions responsible for regulating rent to ensure that accommodation charges are reasonable and comply with the law.

“We will petition the Minister of Education and the appropriate authorities that are responsible for controlling rent in this country. We are a country of laws. We must allow our laws to work. No single individual is bigger or greater than the laws of this country,” he said.

Mr Opare-Addo stressed that the government would engage owners of private hostels to address the situation and ensure that students are not subjected to unreasonable accommodation charges.

“And so, we will make sure that the right things are done. We will have the necessary conversations with owners of hostels, and we will make sure that prices are reasonable for students,” he added.

The Minister also disclosed that the Ministry of Education was engaging private investors to construct additional affordable accommodation facilities on university campuses.

“I also know that the Ministry of Education is in talks with some private members to build more affordable hotels on campus; we will pursue that,” he said.

Ghana News.title: Cristiano Ronaldo marries longtime love Georgina Rodríguez in Portugal
Ghana News.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo is married!

The Portuguese soccer star, 41, tied the knot with his longtime partner, model Georgina Rodríguez, in a civil ceremony on August 11, 2026, in Cascais, Portugal, according to a press release.

The ceremony was a “private and intimate moment” attended by their five children.

Ronaldo shared a photo of the couple’s hands with their wedding bands with the caption: “C❤️G”.

The wedding comes one year after Rodríguez, 32, announced their engagement on Instagram on Aug. 11, 2025.

For the announcement, she shared a picture of her hand over Ronaldo’s, offering a close-up look at her massive, oval-shaped diamond sparkler.

“Sí, quiero. En esta y en todas mis vidas,” Rodríguez wrote in the caption, which translates to, “Yes, I do. In this and in all my lives.”

The couple shares five children: twins Eva Maria and Mateo, 9, daughter Alana, 8, daughter Bella, 4, and 16-year-old son Cristiano Jr., whom Ronaldo welcomed in a previous relationship.

Georgina Rodríguez shares a photo of her engagement ring

Credit: Georgina Rodri­guez/instagram

He and Rodríguez previously announced the death of Bella’s newborn twin brother, Ángel, in April 2022.

Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodríguez with their kids.

Credit: Cristiano Ronaldo/Instagram

Ronaldo first met Rodríguez when she was working as a sales assistant at a Gucci store in 2017. That January, the two made their red carpet debut at the Best FIFA Football Awards in Zurich. By May, they made things Instagram official when Ronaldo posted a photo of himself and Rodríguez.

In Rodríguez’s 2022 Netflix reality series, I Am Georgina, Ronaldo opened up about the early days of their romance.

The athlete said he thought Rodríguez was a “very interesting girl, so much more mature for her age,” but that he didn’t expect the romance to last.

Georgina Rodríguez and Cristiano Ronaldo share a kiss after a game in 2018.

Credit: Alexander Hassenstein - UEFA/UEFA via Getty

He told viewers in confessional footage that he “didn’t think at the beginning that [the relationship] would be this strong, that I would fall in love with her. I didn’t expect it, honestly. But after a while, I felt that she was the woman of my life.”

Reflecting on Ronaldo’s surprise marriage proposal in a December 2025 interview with Elle Spain, Rodríguez shared that she was “shocked” in the moment. “The truth is, when he proposed, it was the last thing on my mind,” she told the magazine.

“It took me a long time to process the enormous stone he gave me. I was so shocked that I left it in my room and didn’t open it in the sunlight until the next day.”

As for her jaw-dropping ring, she declared it “gorgeous,” before joking, “It’s the least he could offer me after 10 years of waiting.”

Ghana News.title: Political parties, judiciary must reform themselves to protect Africa’s democracy – Asiedu Nketia
Ghana News.content:
Johnson Asiedu Nketia

National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketia, has called for fundamental reforms within political parties and the judiciary, arguing that the two institutions cannot protect African democracy if they lack credibility, accountability and public trust.

According to him, political parties must move beyond functioning as electoral machines and become permanent democratic institutions, while the judiciary must remain independent and provide justice that is accessible, impartial, timely and credible.

Mr Asiedu Nketia made the call on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, when he participated in the 2026 Goodluck Jonathan Foundation Democracy Dialogue in Bauchi, Nigeria.

The dialogue was held on the theme: "Beyond Elections: Can Political Parties and the Judiciary Save African Democracy?"

Speaking on the panel on political parties and the judiciary and the need to rebuild trust in democratic institutions, Mr Asiedu Nketia said neither political parties nor the courts could save democracy merely by existing.

"Political parties cannot save democracy when they function only as electoral machines, instruments of patronage or vehicles for individual ambition," he said.

"Courts cannot save democracy when they are inaccessible, slow, inconsistent or perceived to be subject to political influence. Both institutions can defend democracy only when they are themselves credible, accountable, competent and trusted."

Democracy goes beyond elections

Mr Asiedu Nketia said elections only determine who receives the authority to govern and do not, on their own, guarantee that political power will subsequently be exercised lawfully.

He said democracy must also be measured by whether constitutional limits are respected, opposition parties are allowed to operate legitimately and governments remain accountable to citizens between elections.

"Elections determine who receives the authority to govern. They do not, by themselves, determine whether that authority will be exercised lawfully, whether constitutional limits will be respected, whether the opposition will remain legitimate or whether government will improve the lives of the people," he said.

"Democracy is therefore tested not only on election day, but in every decision taken between one election and the next."

Ghana's democratic record

Mr Asiedu Nketia cited Ghana's Fourth Republic as an example of democratic institutionalisation, although he cautioned against complacency.

He noted that Ghana had held nine consecutive general elections since 1992, with four elections—in 2000, 2008, 2016 and 2024—resulting in the transfer of power from one political party to another.

He said the peaceful alternation of power demonstrated that an African governing party could lose an election, hand over power peacefully and subsequently return to government through the ballot box rather than force.

He cited the 2008 presidential election as a particularly important example.

Professor John Evans Atta Mills won the election with 50.23 per cent of the vote against 49.77 per cent for Nana Addo Dankwa Akufo-Addo, a margin of less than one percentage point.

Mr Asiedu Nketia said the ability of political leaders, state institutions and citizens to prevent such a close contest from becoming a national crisis was itself an important democratic achievement.

He also cited the 2016 election, when then-President John Dramani Mahama conceded defeat and oversaw the transition of power, and the 2024 election, when then-Vice-President Mahamudu Bawumia conceded before the formal declaration after his party's collation indicated that the result could not be overturned.

"These concessions were not ceremonial courtesies; they were constitutional contributions," he said.

However, Mr Asiedu Nketia warned that Ghana's democratic record should not lead to complacency.

He pointed to the 2020 election, which resulted in a Parliament comprising 137 members from each of the two major parties and one independent member, but was also marked by election-related violence in which eight people were reportedly killed.

"This reminds us that democratic progress is never irreversible," he said.

Political parties must reform

Mr Asiedu Nketia said political parties had responsibilities beyond winning elections and should not be treated as the private property of founders, financiers, office holders or temporary leaders.

He said parties perform important public and constitutional functions, including recruiting political leaders, developing policy alternatives, organising political participation and connecting citizens to the state.

"A party that demands credible national elections must conduct credible internal elections. A party that condemns authoritarianism in government must tolerate legitimate disagreement within its own structures," he said.

He also called for greater inclusion of women, young people and persons with disabilities in political leadership.

Mr Asiedu Nketia said the growing cost of political participation posed a serious threat to internal party democracy because it could make wealth rather than competence the principal requirement for seeking political office.

He cited research by the Westminster Foundation for Democracy and CDD-Ghana which found that the cost of contesting parliamentary office increased by 59 per cent between the 2012 and 2016 electoral cycles, reaching an average of GH¢389,803.

He further cited a CDD-Ghana study which estimated that a viable parliamentary campaign by 2020, including the cost of maintaining a constituency presence, could require about GH¢4 million.

"When entry into political leadership becomes this expensive, parties risk selecting the wealthiest rather than the most capable, while elected officials may enter office burdened by financiers and expectations of repayment," he said.

Parties need policy and leadership institutions

Mr Asiedu Nketia said political parties should also reclaim their policy development, civic education and leadership training functions.

He proposed permanent research institutions within political parties to develop policies, train candidates and office holders and assess governments formed under their platforms.

"Democracy suffers when public office becomes the first place at which political leaders begin to learn the responsibilities of government," he said.

He also called for measurable progress on the participation of women and young people in political leadership.

He noted that women occupied only 40 of Ghana's 276 parliamentary seats, representing 14.5 per cent, despite making up slightly more than half of the country's population.

He said young people between 15 and 35 constituted 38.2 per cent of Ghana's population, yet no member of the current Parliament was aged 30 or younger at the beginning of the legislature.

Political parties, he argued, must create pathways that allow women and young people to move beyond campaign mobilisation into policy development, party leadership, Parliament and executive responsibility.

Judiciary must win public confidence

Turning to the judiciary, Mr Asiedu Nketia said courts remained indispensable to democracy because political competition inevitably produced disputes involving elections, fundamental rights and constitutional boundaries.

He cited Ghana's presidential election petitions following the 2012 and 2020 elections as examples of how major political disagreements could be transferred from the streets to the courtroom.

The 2012 petition was dismissed by a five-to-four majority after an extended hearing, while the 2020 petition was unanimously dismissed by the Supreme Court.

According to Mr Asiedu Nketia, political actors complied with both decisions despite disagreements over aspects of the proceedings and the reasoning of the court.

He said respect for judicial authority, however, did not require political actors to surrender their right to criticise judicial reasoning.

"Legitimate criticism is part of constitutional democracy; intimidation, threats and personal attacks are not," he said.

He added that judicial independence should not be interpreted as freedom from ethical standards, transparency, consistency or public accountability.

Concerns over access to justice

Mr Asiedu Nketia said public confidence in the judiciary was an issue that could not be ignored.

Citing Afrobarometer's Round 10 findings, he said only 35 per cent of Ghanaians trusted the courts "somewhat" or "a lot".

He said half of respondents were not confident that an ordinary person who had been wronged could obtain justice, while only 37 per cent believed they could afford to take a legal problem to court.

Only 38 per cent believed that a case would be resolved within a reasonable period, he added.

Mr Asiedu Nketia stressed that the figures represented public perceptions rather than judicial findings but said such perceptions had implications for institutional legitimacy.

"Judicial authority cannot depend only on constitutional text; it must also rest on citizens' confidence that justice is accessible, impartial and timely," he said.

Courts must exercise restraint

Mr Asiedu Nketia called for a judiciary that was strong enough to restrain governments, protect opposition parties, defend fundamental rights and enforce constitutional limits.

At the same time, he cautioned courts against becoming "alternative political chambers" or replacing decisions properly entrusted to elected institutions and citizens.

He said judicial courage must therefore be accompanied by restraint.

Proposed reforms

Mr Asiedu Nketia proposed a number of reforms aimed at strengthening democratic institutions.

For political parties, he called for enforceable standards on internal democracy, campaign financing, audited accounts, candidate selection and leadership succession.

He also called for the publication of measurable data on women's and youth participation, measures to reduce the financial barriers to political candidature and the establishment of permanent policy and leadership institutions.

On the judiciary, he advocated transparent criteria for judicial appointments and promotions, the prompt publication of constitutional judgments, stronger legal aid services and the publication of reliable information on court performance.

He also called for political parties, courts, electoral bodies, civil society organisations, the media and academic institutions to engage in dialogue before political crises emerge.

"Dialogue should not begin only when an election dispute threatens national stability," he said.

'Parties and judiciary must reform themselves'

In his concluding remarks, Mr Asiedu Nketia said political parties and the judiciary could contribute significantly to safeguarding democracy in Africa, but only if they were willing to reform themselves.

"Political parties must cease to be seasonal electoral machines and become permanent democratic institutions," he said.

"The judiciary must remain independent of political power while providing remedies that are impartial, accessible, timely and convincingly reasoned."

He argued that the future of African democracy would not be secured merely by conducting more elections but by building institutions that make elections meaningful, governments accountable, constitutional limits effective and peaceful transfers of power normal.

"Political parties must remember that power is temporary and that the state belongs to the people," he said.

"The judiciary must understand that its strongest protection is not the goodwill of political leaders, but the confidence of citizens in its independence and integrity."

Mr Asiedu Nketia said democracy would become durable when political parties respected constitutional limits, courts administered justice without fear or favour, governments delivered tangible improvements in people's lives and citizens remained engaged beyond election day.

"Democracy becomes more than a procedure. It becomes a durable system of public trust, peaceful competition, accountable authority and national development," he said.

Ghana News.title: Luv FM High School Debate: T.I AMASS advances as IBASS makes impressive debut
Ghana News.content:
T.I. Ahmadiyya Senior High School–Kumasi and Ibadur Rahman Academy have advanced to the next round of the 2026 LUV FM Kel-Charcoal High School Debate after impressive victories on Day Two of the competition.

The second day of the competition, held at the Christian Service University, delivered two engaging contests as students showcased their knowledge, critical thinking, confidence and ability to defend their positions under pressure.

The two schools emerged victorious after hard-fought battles against Okomfo Anokye SHS and Mankranso SHS, respectively.

The battle of intellects and fearless debaters continued with two action-packed contests, as emotion met logic in very powerful deliveries.

The opening contest of the day saw Mankranso SHS take on Ibadur Rahman Academy on the motion: “ECG should be privatized.”

Mankranso SHS argued in favor of the motion, while Ibadur Rahman Academy opposed it.

Both sides presented well-structured arguments and backed their positions with facts and logical reasoning. The contest also featured spirited rebuttals, making it a closely watched encounter.

At the end of the contest, however, Ibadur Rahman Academy emerged victorious with 210 points against Mankranso SHS’s 185, winning by a majority decision of the judges.

The victory sent the Ibadur Rahman camp into celebration, with the school’s Patron, Mr. Sabato, expressing confidence in the team’s ability to compete against any opponent in the subsequent stages.

“Today, we have announced to the whole of Ghana that indeed IBASS is here, and we are ready for anyone that comes our way,” he said.

The second contest produced another intriguing battle, with T.I. Amass, Kumasi facing Okomfo Anokye SHS, debating the motion: “MMDCEs should be elected.”

T.I. Amass argued for the motion, while Okomfo Anokye took the opposing position.

The two schools delivered strong arguments and counterarguments, with the rebuttal stage providing some of the most intense moments of the contest.

T.I. Amass, however, eventually established its dominance and secured a 213–192 victory, defeating Okomfo Anokye by a 21-point margin through a unanimous decision of the judges.

The victory will come as a boost to the inaugural champions, who are once again setting their sights on the ultimate prize as they would tell us they are coming for what they believe is truly theirs.

The principal speaker for T.I. Amass made the team’s intentions clear after their victory.

“We are ready for whoever comes our way. We are AMASS, and we are not going down without a fight.”

With the conclusion of Day Two, Ibadur Rahman Academy and T.I. Amass SHS join Kumasi Wesley Girls SHS and Christian Service Senior High School (CHRISSEC) as the first four schools to book their places in the next round.

The competition is expected to intensify as more schools take to the stage to battle for qualification and ultimately the championship.

The 2026 edition of the LUV FM Kel-Charcoal High School Debate continues to provide a platform for students to demonstrate their intellectual ability, public speaking skills and confidence while engaging with topical issues of national interest.

The competition is sponsored by Kelcharcoal Toothpaste, Didi Shito, Bigoo, The Seed Travelz, Serpo Mystical Pen, Verna Mineral Water, Jackson University College, Tamak, St. Ben Jewelry, Otuasekan Community Bank, and New Generation Investment Services.

Ghana News.title: Cyberbullying : When social media becomes a tool for public humiliation
Ghana News.content:
A person can make one mistake in front of twenty people and survive the embarrassment.

Make that same mistake in front of a smartphone camera, however, and the story can become very different.

Within seconds, the video can move from one phone to another. Then it appears on WhatsApp. Someone posts it on TikTok. Another person uploads it to Facebook or X. A caption is added. The comments begin.

People laugh.

People insult.

People share.

People create memes.

And before the person at the centre of the video even understands what is happening, a private moment of embarrassment has become a public spectacle.

This is the frightening reality of cyberbullying in the digital age.

Social media has revolutionised communication. Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, X, WhatsApp and other platforms have made it possible for people to communicate, learn, advertise businesses, build careers and express themselves to audiences far beyond their immediate communities.

But the same technology that gives people a voice can also give cruelty a microphone.

The same smartphone that captures memories can capture someone's most vulnerable moment.

And the same “share” button that spreads useful information can spread humiliation to thousands of people.

Cyberbullying is the deliberate use of digital platforms to insult, threaten, harass, intimidate, embarrass, expose or humiliate another person.

It can happen through comments, private messages, group chats, photographs, videos, memes, fake accounts, edited content, false accusations and the unauthorised sharing of personal information.

It can target almost anyone.

A child.

A university student.

A worker.

A public figure.

A person with a disability.

A person struggling financially.

Someone who made a mistake.

Or simply someone who looks, speaks or thinks differently.

The frightening part is that cyberbullying is increasingly being disguised as entertainment.

We call it a joke.

We call it content.

We call it “cruise.”

We say, “It is just social media.”

But for the person being humiliated, it is not “just social media.”

It is their face.

Their voice.

Their reputation.

Their confidence.

Their dignity.

Their life.

When someone's mistake becomes everybody's entertainment

One of the clearest examples is the mocking of people who make mistakes while speaking.

Imagine a university student standing before a class to give a presentation.

They are nervous.

Their hands may shake.

Their voice may tremble.

They may mispronounce a few words.

They may forget a sentence.

These things happen.

Public speaking is a skill that develops with practice.

Yet instead of receiving encouragement or respectful correction, someone may secretly record the presentation.

The video is uploaded.

A funny caption is added.

The student's pronunciation becomes the subject of jokes.

People who have never met the student begin laughing at them.

Some may even tag friends and encourage them to watch.

The student may return to class the next day knowing that hundreds or thousands of people have seen the video.

The lesson is no longer about the presentation.

It becomes about humiliation.

And the next time that student is asked to speak publicly, they may remember what happened.

They may become afraid to participate.

They may begin questioning their intelligence.

They may decide that silence is safer than making another mistake.

That is how cyberbullying can steal something that cannot easily be measured: confidence.

Not everything that is funny is harmless

We need to have an uncomfortable conversation about humour.

Humour is part of human life.

People laugh.

People joke.

Friends tease each other.

There is nothing inherently wrong with comedy.

The problem begins when the joke depends on another person's humiliation.

If one person is laughing and another is suffering, we should question whether it is really a joke.

The fact that thousands of people find something funny does not make it harmless.

Popularity does not turn cruelty into kindness.

Virality does not make humiliation acceptable.

And a laughing emoji does not erase the pain caused by an insult.

The culture of “content” is making things worse

The competition for views, likes, followers and shares has created a digital environment where almost anything can become content.

Someone falls.

Record it.

Someone cries.

Record it.

Someone is arguing.

Record it.

Someone makes a mistake.

Record it.

Someone is embarrassed.

Record it.

The camera often comes out before compassion does.

This should concern us.

We are becoming a society in which witnessing another person's vulnerable moment can trigger the instinct to document it rather than help.

Instead of asking, “Are you okay?”, someone may ask, “Can I post this?”

Instead of helping a person who has fallen, another person may first reach for a phone.

Instead of protecting someone's dignity, we sometimes protect the opportunity for views.

Technology did not create cruelty, but it has made cruelty easier to distribute.

The crowd behind the screen

Cyberbullying is rarely the work of one person alone.

Sometimes one individual creates the original harmful post, but hundreds or thousands of people participate by sharing it.

This is where bystanders become important.

The person who created the video may have started the humiliation.

But the people who shared it gave the humiliation wings.

The person who wrote the insulting caption started the attack.

But the people who liked and reposted it helped amplify it.

We therefore need to stop thinking that only the original poster is responsible for online harm.

Every user has a choice.

You can share.

You can comment.

You can report.

You can ignore.

Or you can stop the spread.

Anonymity can remove accountability

Another problem is the use of anonymous and fake accounts.

Some people hide behind usernames and profile pictures to say things they would never have the courage to say publicly.

They insult people's bodies.

They attack their families.

They spread rumours.

They threaten people.

They make sexualised comments.

They destroy reputations.

Because they believe they cannot be identified, they behave as though there are no consequences.

But anonymity does not make cruelty less harmful.

A victim still experiences the damage whether or not they know the identity of the person responsible.

This is why online accountability matters.

Cyberbullying can become more dangerous than a joke

Online harassment can also move beyond insults.

It can involve threats, impersonation, spreading false information, exposing private conversations, sharing personal information without permission and distributing intimate or embarrassing material.

These actions can have serious consequences.

A person's reputation can be damaged.

Relationships can collapse.

Employment opportunities can be affected.

Academic life can be disrupted.

A victim may become afraid to leave home or interact socially.

The internet can make a victim feel as though there is nowhere to escape.

Home may not feel safe because the messages are arriving on their phone.

School may not feel safe because classmates have seen the content.

Work may not feel safe because colleagues have shared it.

Even sleep can become difficult because the victim keeps checking what people are saying.

That is not harmless entertainment.

The victim is often blamed

One of the most disturbing reactions to cyberbullying is victim-blaming.

When a private photograph is leaked, people may ask why the victim took the photograph.

When someone is mocked for their appearance, people may tell them to change.

When someone is insulted online, people may say they should simply ignore it.

When an embarrassing video spreads, people may ask why the person behaved that way in the first place.

These responses shift responsibility from the person doing the harm to the person being harmed.

We must reject that thinking.

Someone's mistake does not give others permission to humiliate them.

Someone's appearance does not justify abuse.

Someone's private photograph does not give others the right to distribute it.

Someone's opinion does not make them deserving of threats.

The responsibility for abusive behaviour belongs to the person choosing to engage in it.

Young people need protection, but also education

Children and young people are particularly vulnerable because social media is deeply connected to their social lives.

For many young people, being excluded from an online group can feel like being excluded from their entire social world.

A cruel comment from one person can quickly become a group attack.

A private disagreement can become public.

A rumour can travel through an entire school before a teacher even knows it exists.

Parents therefore need to understand the digital environments their children inhabit.

Schools and universities should not wait until a serious incident occurs before discussing cyberbullying.

Students should be taught about digital citizenship, privacy, consent, responsible sharing and online consequences.

They should also know how and where to seek help.

The goal should not be to frighten young people away from technology.

The goal should be to teach them how to use it responsibly.

Universities have a responsibility

Universities are important spaces for addressing this issue because students spend a significant part of their lives communicating digitally.

A student may be mocked in a class WhatsApp group.

A lecturer's presentation may be secretly recorded.

A student's photograph may be circulated without consent.

A private disagreement may become a campus-wide social media issue.

Institutions should therefore create clear policies and reporting mechanisms for serious online harassment.

Students should know who they can approach.

Cases involving threats, harassment or serious reputational harm should not simply be dismissed as “students being students.”

Young adults also deserve protection from harmful digital behaviour.

Social media companies cannot escape responsibility

The platforms themselves also have a responsibility.

Social media companies benefit from the enormous amount of content users create.

They must therefore continue developing effective systems for reporting harassment, threats, impersonation and harmful content.

Users should have accessible privacy controls.

Reporting mechanisms should be understandable.

Repeated abusive behaviour should receive appropriate attention.

The answer cannot be to place the entire burden on victims.

A victim who is being attacked by hundreds of accounts cannot realistically respond to every comment individually.

Technology created the scale of the problem.

Technology must also be part of the solution.

But the biggest change must happen in us

Ultimately, however, no algorithm can replace basic human decency.

We must decide what kind of internet culture we want.

Do we want a digital environment where people are afraid to speak because every mistake could become viral?

Do we want young people to grow up believing that humiliation is entertainment?

Do we want smartphones to become tools for documenting people's pain instead of helping them?

Or do we want social media to be a space for learning, creativity, connection and responsible expression?

The answer depends partly on the choices we make every day.

Every share contributes to the culture.

Every comment contributes to the culture.

Every like contributes to the culture.

Every time we refuse to participate, we also contribute to the culture.

We need to change what we reward

There is a reason humiliating content spreads so quickly.

It attracts attention.

And attention has become a form of currency online.

The more outrageous the content, the more reactions it may receive.

The more embarrassing the moment, the more people may want to watch.

This creates an uncomfortable incentive structure.

If cruelty brings views, some people will produce cruelty.

If humiliation brings followers, some people will pursue humiliation.

If insults generate engagement, some people will continue insulting others.

We therefore need to become more intentional about what we reward with our attention.

Not everything that goes viral deserves to be consumed.

Not everything that is trending deserves a share.

And not everything that makes us laugh deserves to remain online.

Sometimes the most responsible thing a social media user can do is simply not participate.

Correction should not become humiliation

There is nothing wrong with correcting mistakes.

If someone mispronounces a word, teach them.

If someone uses incorrect grammar, correct them respectfully.

If someone shares false information, provide accurate information.

If someone expresses an unpopular opinion, challenge the argument rather than attacking the person.

The purpose of correction should be improvement.

When correction becomes humiliation, learning disappears.

A person who is publicly mocked for making a mistake may become afraid to make another attempt.

That does not make society better.

It creates people who are afraid to speak.

And a society in which people are afraid to speak, ask questions and learn from mistakes is not a healthy society.

What should victims do?

Victims of cyberbullying should not be made to feel that they caused the abuse.

Where possible, they should avoid engaging endlessly with abusive accounts.

They can preserve evidence of serious harassment, block abusive users and use platform reporting tools.

Where threats or serious harassment are involved, appropriate authorities or trusted support systems should be considered.

Most importantly, victims should not suffer in isolation.

A person who is being publicly humiliated needs support, not another lecture about what they should have done differently.

Friends and family can make an enormous difference simply by listening and standing with the person.

The bystander has power

We often talk about bullies and victims.

But there is another important group: the audience.

The audience decides whether harmful content dies quickly or travels widely.

The audience decides whether an insult receives encouragement or silence.

The audience decides whether a person's embarrassment becomes a national joke or disappears into the internet.

This means that every social media user has some responsibility.

We do not have to become heroes.

Sometimes we simply need to refuse to participate.

Do not share the humiliating video.

Do not add the insulting comment.

Do not forward the private photograph.

Do not laugh at someone's pain simply because everyone else is laughing.

Do not turn another person's worst moment into your entertainment.

Social media should not punish people for being human

People will make mistakes.

They will stumble over words.

They will forget things.

They will dress differently.

They will express unpopular opinions.

They will sometimes behave awkwardly.

They will fail.

They will learn.

They will grow.

That is what being human means.

If every mistake is recorded and every weakness is exposed, we create a society where people are constantly performing instead of genuinely living.

Everyone becomes afraid of being watched.

Everyone becomes afraid of being judged.

Everyone becomes afraid that one bad moment could define them forever.

That is not freedom.

That is digital fear.

We must build a culture where people can make mistakes without becoming targets.

The conversation must become national

Cyberbullying should no longer be treated as merely a social media problem.

It intersects with education, mental wellbeing, privacy, child protection, digital literacy, human dignity and responsible citizenship.

Parents must talk about it.

Schools must teach about it.

Universities must address it.

Media organisations must discuss it.

Influencers must model responsible behaviour.

Technology companies must strengthen protections.

And social media users must understand that their actions have consequences.

The solution begins with a simple principle:

Just because you can post something does not mean you should.

Technology gives us the ability to reach millions.

It does not give us the right to destroy someone's dignity.

Before posting, commenting, recording or sharing, we should pause and ask:

Is this true?

Is this necessary?

Is this respectful?

Would I want this done to me?

And if the answer is no, perhaps the best button to press is not “share.”

It is “delete.”

Because behind every username is a human being.

Behind every photograph is a person.

Behind every embarrassing video is someone who may be trying desperately to forget what happened.

The internet may move quickly, but human emotions do not always heal at the same speed.

A cruel comment may take five seconds to write.

A humiliating video may take ten seconds to upload.

A share may take one second.

But the damage can last for years.

So the next time we see someone being mocked online, let us not ask only, “Is this funny?”

Let us ask:

“What if this were me?”

Social media should be a place where people connect, learn, create and express themselves—not a digital courtroom where ordinary human mistakes are punished before millions of spectators.

We cannot control everything that appears on the internet.

But we can control what we contribute to it.

And perhaps the most powerful way to fight cyberbullying is to remember something that technology can never erase:

There is a human being behind the screen.

Do not turn someone's mistake into your entertainment.

Do not turn their pain into your content.

And do not let the click of a button become the beginning of someone's suffering.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.title: Russian authorities detain suspect over St. Petersburg cafe blast
World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”
