World.title: New Coral Species Found Off Costa Rica Gets a Name From Tolkien’s Elvish
World.content:
A bright yellow coral that grows like a small tree on the flanks of Costa Rica’s underwater mountains has turned out to be so unlike anything else in the ocean that scientists had to build a new branch of the coral family tree to hold it. The animal has been named Laurinque elenya, and its formal description does something researchers rarely get to do in a single paper. It establishes a new species, a new genus and an entirely new family, Laurinqueidae, all at once.

The study was published in the open-access journal ZooKeys in late June and announced by the publisher this week. It was led by Odalisca Breedy, an octocoral specialist at the Universidad de Costa Rica, working with an international team that included researchers from the Smithsonian Institution’s National Museum of Natural History.

The colonies grow to more than a meter (3.3 feet) tall and were collected between 360 and 529 meters (1,180 and 1,735 feet) below the surface. That is far below the reach of any recreational diver, in a stretch of the Pacific that has been surveyed only a handful of times. Specimens came up during two expeditions, in 2019 and 2023, using the remotely operated vehicle SuBastian deployed from the research vessels Falkor and Falkor (too), both operated by the Schmidt Ocean Institute.

The dives covered seamounts off the insular shelf of Isla del Coco and three geological features along Costa Rica’s Pacific margin. What the cameras found on those rocky outcrops is the reason for the coral’s unusual name. The rock was almost completely carpeted in brittle stars, and the golden colonies rose out of that shimmering layer like lit-up trees.

Breedy and her co-authors turned to Quenya, the Elvish language J.R.R. Tolkien invented for The Lord of the Rings and The Silmarillion. The genus name comes from Laurinquë, meaning golden tree, for the colonies’ color and branching shape. The species name, elenya, means stellar or of the stars, a reference to the brittle star fields the coral was growing in.

Placing the coral in the tree of life proved considerably harder than naming it. The team sequenced three genes routinely used to sort octocorals into families, and each one pointed to a different, unrelated family, an unusually stark disagreement. To break the tie, the researchers ran a phylogenomic analysis using hundreds of genes at once. That result was unambiguous.

The coral sits in its own lineage, closest to the family Eunicellidae but different enough in both genetics and anatomy that neither that family nor any other could accommodate it. Breedy said she first saw the octocoral garden in 2019 and was struck by the beauty of the landscape, which later inspired the Elvish name. Her early look at the specimens’ physical structure told her something was off.

She said “it was something very different that I could not match” against known groups, and only the molecular work done after the 2023 collection settled where it belonged. The expeditions were supported by the Schmidt Ocean Institute and a National Geographic Society research grant. The find lands in waters that already carry heavy conservation weight.

Isla del Coco is a national park and a UNESCO World Heritage site, and the government significantly enlarged the protected area around it at the end of 2021. Deep coral gardens like this one are classified as vulnerable marine ecosystems. They build complex three-dimensional structure on otherwise bare rock, which becomes habitat for a wide range of other deep-sea animals, and they recover very slowly from physical damage such as bottom contact from fishing gear.

The discovery adds to a lengthening list of species being pulled out of Costa Rican waters for the first time. In June, researchers described a new deep-sea ghost shark from the Pacific, and in May a jaguar-patterned marine worm was named from a beach in Santa Rosa National Park.

On land the pace has been similar, with a new frog described from the streams of the Los Santos coffee region and a new tree species added to the national record from the Guanacaste mountains.

Roughly two-thirds of the planet’s surface lies under deep ocean, and the overwhelming majority of it has never been looked at directly. For a country that has built much of its international identity on biodiversity, the coral is a reminder that a significant share of that biodiversity sits hundreds of kilometers offshore and hundreds of meters down, in places almost nobody has seen.

World.title: Rescue Center Raises $20,000 to Stop Wildlife Electrocutions
World.content:
The Jaguar Rescue Center has finished a fundraising campaign with the organization Ma Earth that raised $20,000 to insulate 50 electrical transformers in Costa Rica’s South Caribbean, in an effort to reduce wildlife electrocutions in the region.

The money will buy insulation material that the Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad will install at the locations recording the most electrocutions, known as hot spots. The center, which operates near Puerto Viejo de Talamanca in Limón province, began the project 17 years ago after it started receiving electrocuted primates and sloths, which it describes as among the most difficult rescues it handles.

Encar García, who founded the center with biologist Sandro Alviani, said these accidents almost always end in euthanasia, amputation or months of recovery, and frequently leave orphaned young when a mother is electrocuted. In one recent week the center received seven electrocuted animals.

The scale of the problem extends well beyond the Caribbean. International Animal Rescue Costa Rica reports close to 100 electrocuted animals a year in the Nosara area alone, while the Jaguar Rescue Center took in 53 animals in 2024. Rescue centers around Costa Rica receive animals affected by electrical discharge every three to five days, and roughly 90% of electrocuted animals die.

The voltages involved explain why. A domestic shock at 110 volts is painful to a person; animals on distribution lines encounter between 2,500 and 35,000 volts, according to Francisco Sánchez, veterinary director at International Animal Rescue. The animals most often affected are howler monkeys, sloths and tamanduas, species that use power lines as improvised bridges because habitat fragmentation has left them without continuous canopy to travel through. They do not distinguish between a vine and a cable.

García said the center has imported materials from the United States to test which types of insulation perform best on transformers, working alongside the ICE to solve the specific problem of sloths reaching across contact plates with their long arms. She described the two organizations as pioneers in that testing, and said the collaboration has produced substantial improvement.

Electrocutions nevertheless continue to rise, she said, because no legislation requires new construction to use insulated or buried cable. The absence of a regulatory plan governing development in the South Caribbean compounds the problem, leaving the pace of new electrical infrastructure effectively unmanaged in one of the country’s fastest-growing tourism corridors.

A legal instrument already exists on paper. Executive Decree No. 44329, published in January 2024, requires all electrical utilities to prevent and mitigate wildlife deaths on their networks, setting out measures including insulation on cabling and transformers, metal cones to block access to lines, aerial wildlife crossings, tree pruning and the tallying of animal-related faults to identify priority zones. Conservation organizations campaigning under the banner “Esto NO es Pura Vida” have said implementation has been close to nonexistent more than a year after the decree took effect.

Separately, the Legislative Assembly approved a wildlife crossings bill in second debate by 56 votes to zero. Another bill, introduced in 2022 by former Frente Amplio legislator Ariel Robles, adds a new Article 31 bis to the Organic Environmental Law and requires all public infrastructure, new or existing, to guarantee safe passage for wildlife where technical evidence shows roads are fragmenting habitat. The measure becomes law once signed at Casa Presidencial, after which the Sistema Nacional de Áreas de Conservación will have 24 months to begin identifying natural crossing points on roads already in operation.

There is evidence the combined approach works. Research by Inés Azofeifa and Tremaine Gregory found that after 111 aerial crossings were installed between 2015 and 2021 alongside insulated cabling at Playa Hermosa in Guanacaste, the local mantled howler monkey population rose from 59 to 99 individuals while annual deaths fell from five to one.

The Jaguar Rescue Center receives no government funding and operates on donations, community support and entrance fees, taking in around 1,000 animals a year. This is not its first campaign to pay for insulation on transformers and lines, and and on current evidence it will not be its last.

World.title: International News: Colombia Earthquake death toll tops 250 as rescuers search for survivors
World.content:
International News: Colombia Earthquake death toll tops 250 as rescuers search for survivors

By Zoila Palma: Rescue crews in western Colombia continued searching through mountains of rubble on Tuesday after a powerful 7.4-magnitude earthquake devastated the country’s coffee-growing region.

The death toll had risen to at least 254 people, according to reports from affected cities, with 101 deaths recorded in Pereira and 95 in Cali, Reuters report.

The earthquake, described as the most devastating to strike Colombia this century, struck early Monday and damaged or destroyed apartment buildings, homes, schools and health centers.

Rescue workers used cranes, excavators and their bare hands to search for survivors, while authorities called for silence in some areas so they could listen for people trapped beneath the rubble. Nearly 100 aftershocks had been recorded by early Tuesday.

Thousands of people were left homeless, while electricity, water, healthcare and telephone services remained disrupted in several communities. Indigenous communities in the Pacific-facing Chocó region near the epicenter were particularly affected, with damage to roads and infrastructure complicating rescue and relief operations.

Six airports were also temporarily closed because of earthquake-related damage.

President Abelardo De La Espriella visited affected areas and pledged economic assistance to families who lost their homes.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency assistance, while the Inter-American Development Bank said $50 million was immediately available for reconstruction support if requested.

World.title: Belize Forest Department urges responsible behavior around crocodiles
World.content:
Belize Forest Department urges responsible behavior around crocodiles

By Zoila Palma: The Belize Forest Department (BFD), in collaboration with ACES Wildlife Rescue and the Crocodile Research Coalition (CRC), is the public to refrain from feeding, approaching, or interacting with crocodiles in their natural habitat.

The advisory follows recent reports and social media posts involving human-crocodile interactions, including a recent incident in Caye Caulker Village. While no physical contact or injury was observed in that particular incident, it underscores the importance of responsible behaviour in areas where crocodiles are present.

Crocodiles are native to Belize and naturally inhabit mangroves, lagoons, wetlands, rivers and coastal areas. As human activity and development increasingly overlap with natural crocodile habitat, encounters between people and wildlife may occur. Public awareness and responsible behaviour are therefore important to protecting both people and crocodiles.

“Of particular concern are reports of crocodiles being intentionally fed or encouraged to approach people. The Forest Department strongly reminds the public that crocodiles should never be fed, approached, touched, provoked or encouraged to interact with people,” the Forest Department said.

Feeding crocodiles, whether directly or indirectly, can alter their natural behaviour, cause them to associate people with food and increase the potential for negative human-crocodile interactions. Residents, visitors, and businesses are encouraged to support responsible wildlife viewing practices that maintain a safe distance and do not involve feeding, attracting, or attempting to interact with crocodiles in their environment or habitat.

The public is urged to never feed, approach, touch or attempt to capture a crocodile.

You must also avoid swimming at night or in mangrove areas and other locations where crocodiles are known to occur; and keep children and pets at a safe distance from the water’s edge where crocodiles are present.

The Forest Department encourages the public to make use of these reporting channels so that situations can be properly assessed, and the appropriate response determined.

The Belize Forest Department, ACES Wildlife Rescue and CRC have also agreed to undertake additional measures to strengthen public awareness and support the existing emergency response and reporting system.

These measures will include increased public education on crocodile safety and responsible coexistence, engagement with communities and stakeholders, and the installation of appropriate crocodile safety and warning signage at strategic locations.

Community meetings will also be held with residents and stakeholders in Caye Caulker Village to discuss crocodile behaviour, safety and community concerns.

World.title: Cabinet receives presentations from Acquisition Stakeholders
World.content:
Cabinet receives presentations from Acquisition Stakeholders

By Zoila Palma: The Government of Belize noted that as part of the process to determine its position on the proposed acquisition of Smart/Speednet Communications Ltd. by Belize Telemedia Limited (BTL), Cabinet invited stakeholders to make presentations on the proposed acquisition.

At today’s meeting with the Belize Social Security Board, the Public Utilities Commission and BTL will present to Cabinet.

On Thursday, August 13, 2026, the Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry and the National Trade Union Congress of Belize (NTUCB) will be invited to make presentations to the Cabinet.

Cabinet said that following these presentations, cabinet will deliberate at its meeting on August 18 and inform on its position on the matter.

World.title: International News: Alleged murder plot against Messi revealed in police report
World.content:
International News: Alleged murder plot against Messi revealed in police report

By Zoila Palma: Football superstar Lionel Messi was reportedly the target of multiple serious threats during the 2026 World Cup, including an alleged plot to kill him inside a stadium, according to a police report reviewed by Spanish newspaper Marca.

The report detailed security threats investigated by U.S. authorities during the tournament, with Messi reportedly receiving more death threats than any other footballer named.

One alleged threat involved plans to enter a stadium with homemade explosives and an AR-15 rifle, while another suspect reportedly threatened to attack Messi during Argentina’s group-stage match against Jordan.

Ahead of Argentina’s match against Egypt, another suspect allegedly posted online that he planned to enter Atlanta Stadium and kill Messi using explosives.

Authorities reportedly took the threat seriously and searched the stadium with sniffer dogs, including checks of bins and other areas, but no explosives were found.

Messi was not the only football star reportedly targeted during the tournament.

Cristiano Ronaldo also faced security concerns, while French referee François Letexier reportedly received more than 6,000 hate messages following the controversial Argentina-Egypt match.

World.title: When the pendulum swings
World.content:
When the pendulum swings

The views expressed in this article are those of the writer and not necessarily those of Breaking Belize News.

Dr. Philip Castillo: In any two party democracy, the pendulum eventually swings. Key word…eventually. But what makes it swing?

Focus on the comparatively more recent “Pendulum Swing” General Elections and recall the tremendous outpouring of pure national joy that accompanied such elections in Belize. Mr. Said Musa and the PUP won the pendulum swing General Elections in 1998 with a national total of 59.3% of votes and was the first to repeat in 2003 with a national total of 52.8%. In the subsequent five year span from 2003 to 2008, the pendulum again swung such that the PUP lost badly in 2008, when they obtained only obtained 40.9% of the votes. What made the pendulum swing? Was it one issue? A combination of several issues? American pollsters coin the phrase “wedge issue” to focus on a defining issue that motivates single issue voters or brings out less motivated and occasional voters. Was there a wedge issue in 2008 that “moved the needle”? This is another phrase used by pollsters to describe a seismic shift in political fortunes.

Mr. Dean Barrow and the UDP won the pendulum swing national elections in 2008, with 56.3% of the national vote and kept wining for three consecutive elections until defeat in 2020. The same questions need to be asked. What made the pendulum swing? Was it one issue? A combination of several issues? Was there a wedge issue in 2020?

Table 1

Election Year % PUP votes % UDP votes % alternate party votes Voter Turnout (%) Comments Possible Reason for Pendulum Swing 1993 51.2 48.7 .06 71.6 1998* 59.3 39.2 0.9 90.1 Pendulum Swing to PUP. Note INCREASE in % votes for PUP, DECREASE in % votes for UDP & massive INCREASE in voter turnout. Retrenchment?? Introduction of VAT?? Economic Citizenship Programme?? 2003 52.8 45.2 1.3 79.5 Start of 2nd term for PUP 2008* 40.9 56.3 2.1% 77.2 Pendulum Swing to UDP. Note double digit DECREASE in % votes for PUP & double digit INCREASE in % votes for UDP. Corruption/Malfeasance?? PUP infighting – Gang of Seven?? Superbond?? Privatization of national assets?? BTL issues?? Ministerial misconduct?? 2012 NA NA NA 73.2 Start of 2nd term for UDP 2015 47.3 50.0 1.7 72.7 Start of 3rd term for UDP 2020* 58.9 38.3 1.5 81.9 Pendulum Swing to PUP. Note double digit INCREASE in % votes for PUP, double digit DECREASE in % votes for UDP & INCREASE in voter turnout. Corruption/Malfeasance?? UDP infighting & succession squabbles?? Covid Restrictions?? Ministerial misconduct?? 2025** 66.6 28.9** 2.5 65.0 **The UDP % represent the combined totals of the Tracey & Shyne factions of the party .

Source: https://elections.gov.bz/general-election-results/

In general, while there are many issues that motivate a typical Belizean voter, my polls have found that generally high on their list — in no particular order are their economic situation, perceptions of corruption/malfeasance in government, candidate quality, party loyalty and family connections. Money is important because, among other things, it is needed to motivate the base, entice the less committed and dole out favours, including outright bribery. Note the report from BelPri on money in Belizean politics. https://heyzine.com/flip-book/8bd36f9fb4.html

Incumbency does confer advantages and in our politics, one such advantage is that it allows the incumbent to use public resources for partisan electoral advantage. We are also now aware of chicanery in the electoral process whereby voters form one constituency are transferred to another constituency. Both parties have safe houses where many voters officially reside. Both parties also activate bacon houses where benefits are doled out to partisan supporters. Money, in multiples of thousands, is required to undertake these activities.

But money also has its limitations due to what economists refer to as diminishing returns. After all, cash rich incumbent governments and cash rich individual politicians have lost, sometimes badly. In Belize, Opposition politicians are known to advise voters to “Take dem money and still vote dem out.” This is tacit acknowledgement that incumbents have money and resources, which voters are encouraged to take accept, while simultaneously voting against said incumbent. Rinse and repeat when governments change.

Fast forward to Mr. John Briceno and the PUP’s pendulum-swing victory in 2020. A victory that was repeatedly on a similar scale in 2025, facing a divided Opposition. The next set of elections that will serve as a referendum on Mr. Briceno’s government are the municipals slated for next year 2027, then the village councils slated for the following year 2028. But will the pendulum swing? Will the needle move? Voter turnout may provide a guide.

But Approval Ratings would likely provide a more reliable guide. My polling revealed an approval rating of 21.8% for the PM in Dangriga in February 2026. A month later in March my polls revealed an approval rating of 39.1% for the PM in Belmopan. Admittedly approval ratings are time and location specific, but I daresay, in the absence of actual elections, approval ratings polls of the Prime Minister, if regularly undertaken and countrywide in scope, would definitely provide an excellent indicator of any pendulum swing. And reasons that may cause any such swing?

Listen to the UDP talk shows. Their big issue is corruption/malfeasance in Government. Then listen to the PUP talk show, and be regaled with the corruption/malfeasance issues that doomed the UDP in 2020 and be reminded that some players are still around. Is corruption/malfeasance a wedge issue and will it cause any pendulum swing?

It is glaringly obvious, that for its own survival, the PUP must meaningfully address the burgeoning stench of the corruption/malfeasance issue surrounding government’s procurement and payment processes. Particularly distressing is the report of unsuitable guns to our soldiers. One indicator that the PUP has effectively dealt with this issue is actually ensuring transparency, due process and enhanced governance such that any leaks in any procurement and payment processes are no longer necessary.

But until then, expect the UDP to keep riding the corruption horse for as long as they can. But will that cause the pendulum to swing? Will that move the needle? And if so, would the movement be sufficient to make a meaningful difference?

At this time, focusing on Belmopan is most appropriate because both election and polling data exists. In 2020, then novice politician Mr. Oscar Mira won 60% of the votes to defeat veteran incumbent Mr. John Saldivar. Five years later, Mr. Mira again defeated Mr. Saldivar, and this time Mr. Mira’s voting percentage had upped to 65%. Exactly one year later in March 2026, Castillo Poll # 2 recorded an approval rating of Mr. Mira at 67.5%. Fast forward couple months later to June 2026 and Mr. Mira is among the central figures in the procurement debacle and has officially obtained a leave of absence from his Cabinet duties as Minister of Home Affairs.

The above are all known and undisputed facts. There are many other known and undisputed facts regarding questionable procurement and associated payment practices involving other senior government officials. Now adding to the above, it was announced last week that the national telecoms company (BTL/Digi) is purchasing its rival (SMART) thus re-creating a de facto monopoly in the all-important telecommunications sector. Several sectors of society have mobilized in opposition.

But focusing specifically on future political outcomes, the questions are: Can any of the above be regarded as wedge issues? Has the pendulum swung? Has the needle started to move? And if so, by how much? Would issues that are of intense interest to popular media outlets, talk show hosts, political operatives, the business and social sectors and the trade unions register as major concerns to actual voters? Or as an ephemeral blowing over of a “lee breeze?”

The President of Belize’s largest and most powerful commercial entity, Mr. Giacomo Sanchez of the Belize Chamber of Commerce and Industry, when questioned specifically on the BTL acquisition mentioned the high degree of political apathy with the following statement:

Giacomo Sanchez, President, BCCI

“Well, the public should push back. However, there’s only a few people in the know that will feel the way we feel. However, I mean, just about 90% of Belizeans could care less.” https://www.7newsbelize.com/index.php#story8

Reverting back to Mr. Mira, from a objectively polled approval rating of 67.5% in March, for his electoral fortunes to be jeopardized, his approval rating would have to fall by at least 18 percentage points to hover below 50%. But possibly even more than 18%, to account for what is regarded as the statistical margin of error. A national Approval Rating for the Prime Minister is unknown.

And so then, while the political capital of the incumbent Government has diminished, to what extent has the pendulum swung? Has the needle moved sufficiently to make a difference? These are prime examples of known unknowns.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Dr. Philip Castillo is a development economist and an independent pollster. Send comments to [email protected]

World.title: Taiwan opens applications for 2026 Global Pathfinders Initiative
World.content:
Taiwan opens applications for 2026 Global Pathfinders Initiative

By Zoila Palma: The Taiwan Embassy in Belize is inviting young Belizeans to apply for the 2026 Taiwan Global Pathfinders Initiative, a flagship program aimed at strengthening youth exchanges and creating opportunities for Belizean participants to gain international exposure.

Selected participants will travel to Taiwan for a fully sponsored one-month program in October 2026. The initiative, launched by Taiwan’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Ministry of Education, will provide participants with an opportunity to explore areas of cooperation and develop ideas connected to Belize’s future development.

Applicants are invited to submit proposals under one of two themes: Sustainable Tourism or New Energy and Carbon Credit Cooperation. Preference will be given to applicants who have not previously travelled to Taiwan or abroad, with up to six Belizean candidates expected to be selected for this year’s program.

The deadline for applications is August 20, 2026.

Applicants must submit all required documents in person at Taiwan Embassy.

World.title: Scarlet Macaws released back into wild in Cayo
World.content:
Scarlet Macaws released back into wild in Cayo

By Zoila Palma: Fifteen scarlet macaws were released into the wild in the Cayo District on August 10, 2026, following a rehabilitation and monitoring effort led by Friends for Conservation and Development (FCD) in collaboration with the Forest Department.

The parrots had been rescued and placed at a rehabilitation facility, where they remained for approximately 100 days before being prepared for release.

According to FCD, the macaws were placed at the facility because of the high risk of being poached or dying when three chicks are found in a nesting cavity. The birds were cared for under a strict protocol established by the Forest Department. After being rescued, they were fed and eventually transferred to a flight cage, where they developed their flying skills and prepared for survival in the wild.

On Monday morning, the cage was opened and the macaws were allowed to return to their natural environment. The birds initially gathered to feed on fruits and nuts before gradually flying out of the flight cage. While some flew longer distances, others remained closer to the release site as they adjusted to their surroundings.

FCD said its Research Unit has also been conducting biological monitoring of scarlet macaws since early March. The monitoring focuses on the species’ natural cavities and helps researchers maintain a presence around nesting sites while ensuring that chicks are developing safely until they are ready to leave the nest. Personnel presence also helps deter poachers, although FCD reported that two chicks were lost to poachers this year.

FCD noted that illegal wildlife trade remains a significant threat to scarlet macaws.

FCD and the Forest Department maintain a binational task force that shares information and coordinates interventions to address wildlife trafficking. However, the organizations say it remains difficult to determine the exact number of macaws lost to the illegal trade each year, with some poached birds reportedly taken into Guatemala by Guatemalan “guauqeros,” or macaw poachers.

The release of the 15 macaws marks another important milestone in ongoing efforts to increase Belize’s scarlet macaw population, which FCD says has now surpassed 500 individuals.

During the last national survey, approximately 350 individual parrots were known to be present in the country. FCD says that while the population appears to be expanding, continued monitoring, protection and conservation efforts remain essential to safeguard the species.

World.title: World Meteorological Organization: July among hottest on record as extreme weather intensifies globally
World.content:
World Meteorological Organization: July among hottest on record as extreme weather intensifies globally

By Zoila Palma: The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) says July was marked by extreme weather conditions around the world, with record ocean temperatures, intense heat, drought, wildfires and flooding continuing into August. The latest assessment highlights the growing impacts of a warming climate across several regions.

July was the second-warmest July ever recorded, tied with July 2024, with global temperatures reaching 1.47°C above the pre-industrial average. Western Europe experienced its hottest June-July period on record, with four heatwaves recorded since May, according to the Copernicus EU Climate Change Service.

Ocean temperatures also reached unprecedented levels, with global sea surface temperatures recording their highest July levels on record. Exceptionally warm conditions were reported across the tropical Pacific as El Niño strengthens, while record-high sea temperatures and widespread marine heatwaves affected coastal communities and ecosystems in the Atlantic and western Mediterranean.

Meanwhile, drought conditions intensified across Western Europe, where major rivers including the Seine, Rhine and Danube recorded exceptionally low water flows.

Drier-than-average conditions were also reported in parts of North America, Africa, Asia and South America, while Western Europe experienced exceptional wildfire activity. Major fires were also reported in parts of the western United States and Canada.

At the same time, intense monsoon rains triggered flooding across parts of West Africa and South and Southeast Asia, with India and other countries facing increased risks of flash floods and landslides.

Typhoon Dolphin, an unusually long-lasting storm that formed in late July, also prompted mass evacuations and emergency response efforts in China ahead of its landfall on August 7, highlighting the continuing threat of extreme weather as August unfolds.

World.title: Committing to CCJ would be reckless, says Tavares-Finson
World.content:
Tom Tavares Finson

President of the Jamaican Senate, King’s Counsel Tom Tavares-Finson says it would be extremely reckless for Jamaica to commit to the Caribbean Court of Justice (CCJ) as its final appellate court given the turmoil currently gripping the institution.

The Trinidad Express reported earlier this week a series of allegations made by judges of the CCJ, including allegations of dictatorial tendencies in the running of the court and a series of inter-personal conflict.

Tavares-Finson says no less than a public enquiry is required to deal with the issues facing the CCJ.

While acknowledging that inter-personal conflicts is not unusual for a court, he said the allegation surrounding the convening of panels to achieve pre-desired outcomes is troubling and must be treated seriously.

Tavares-Finson says the Opposition People’s National Party, whose insistence that Jamaica must accept the CCJ as its final appellate court has stalled the island’s constitutional reform process, should state clearly whether it maintains its position despite the turmoil which has gripped the regional court.

World.title: WATCH: 20 families homeless after early morning demolition in Trelawny
World.content:
Flattened structures in Coopers Pen, Trelawny after a demolition crew tore down 20 housing units in the area on Tuesday, August 11, 2026. (Photo: Horace Hines)

TRELAWNY, Jamaica — Some 20 families in Coopers Pen, Trelawny, have been left homeless after a demolition team reportedly tore down about 20 housing units in an early-morning operation Tuesday.

The residents say they have been before the courts since 2009 for the parcel of land that some say they have occupied for more than three decades.

Residents said the demolition crew arrived on the parcel of land shortly after 3:30 am, catching them off guard and leaving little time to save their belongings.

The team reportedly arrived with two excavators, sledgehammers, pickaxes and other equipment, and was accompanied by a strong contingent of police personnel.

Residents said they received no prior warning before the demolition began.

They also claimed that, before leaving the area, members of the demolition team warned that they would return in the coming weeks to continue the operation.

World.title: Tougher water fines
World.content:
Water level in the Mona reservoir last week.

SEVEN parishes will face a water prohibition from Monday, August 17 as the Government moves to tighten restrictions amid worsening drought conditions.

At the same time, Minister of Water, Environment and Climate Change Matthew Samuda is set to approach the executive and legislature to punish violators with stiffer fines.

“As we had to do after the first incident that took place with Rio Cobre, where we had to shift the fine, we now have to take the same approach with fines in relation to water prohibition,” Samuda told the Jamaica Observer on Monday.

“Because of the present forecast and warning associated with El Niño, we will have to move with unprecedented speed, and we will have to engage first the Cabinet and then Parliament in the coming weeks to facilitate this,” Samuda added.

On Monday, Samuda’s ministry, through the National Water Commission (NWC), announced that the water prohibition orders will apply to Kingston, St Andrew, St Thomas, St Mary, Portland, St Ann, and St Catherine and will remain in force until further notice.

“Under the orders, no person shall use or cause water supplied by the NWC to be used for non-essential or unusual purposes. Prohibited activities include:

• irrigation or watering of gardens, lawns, grounds, and farms;

• refilling or supplying of ponds or swimming pools and/or for use other than normal domestic services such as drinking, cooking, washing, bathing, and sanitation;

• washing of vehicles by the use of a hose;

• watering or washing of roadways, pavements, paths, garages, or out-rooms;

• any activity requiring excessive or unusual quantities of water,” the ministry release stated.

The ministry said the decision followed a high-level stakeholder meeting earlier Monday with the NWC and the Meteorological Service, which confirmed that rainfall levels remain critically low and temperatures continue to soar.

Underscoring the necessity of the measure, Samuda said, “We understand that there is some disproportionate economic impact on commercial operations, such as car washes, and we have not taken this decision lightly. Ultimately, our priority is to maintain supply to critical services, especially schools, as we prepare for the September reopening.”

He further advised that sanctions will be applied to individuals and entities found in breach of the prohibition order, noting “these penalties are intended to ensure compliance and protect the integrity of Jamaica’s water supply during this critical period”.

The current fine for breaching an NWC prohibition order is $1,000. Failure to pay the court-ordered fine results in imprisonment for up to 30 days.

Samuda’s reference to the Rio Cobre was the action taken by the Government after chemical spills that resulted in fish kills that affected several species and impacted other aquatic organisms four years ago.

In January 2025 he successfully piloted a Bill in the House of Representatives which approved amendments to the Natural Resources Conservation Authority (NRCA) Act and the Wild Life Protection Act to allow for significant increases in fines and related custodial sentences.

Under the Acts, depending on the severity of the offence, as adjudicated by the Supreme Court, corporate bodies may now be subject to a fine of approximately $10 million, individuals in breach of the Acts may face a fine of up to $5 million or serve a term of imprisonment up to five years, subject to the jurisdiction of the parish courts.

On Monday, Samuda told the Observer that the request he will be taking to Cabinet and Parliament is to “move the fines in line with what was done for bodies corporate and individuals under the NRCA Act breaches.

The naturally-occurring El Niño climate pattern, which began in June and is expected to peak later this year, has already amplified unprecedented temperatures across the world.

Some 33 countries recorded their hottest July since records began, according to a detailed analysis of billions of data points from Copernicus’s ERA5 climate model.

The severe drought has triggered food security concerns worldwide.

Last week, the United Nations World Food Programme said that Central America is expected to be the region hardest hit in terms of the relative increase in food insecurity.

Including the Caribbean, the agency estimates that an additional 16 million people could face food insecurity by the end of 2027.

World.title: Who hurt the child?
World.content:
AN announcement by the Child Protection and Family Services Agency (CPFSA) that it is fast-tracking the installation of security cameras at Glenhope Place of Safety, even as it probes the injuries suffered by a one-year-old boy who had been in its care, has been welcomed by attorney Denise Hinson who is adamant that somebody needs to be held accountable for how the child came to be injured in such a manner.

“The questions still need to be answered. This should not be pushed under the rug. I’m angry, and I think that someone needs to explain why a one-year-old defenceless child, a Jamaican child, looks as if he was in an MMA (mixed martial arts) fight,” Hinson told the Jamaica Observer on Monday.

The attorney is representing the mother of the child who is before the court for immigration issues.

She said the child’s injuries captivated the attention of the St Catherine Parish Court last Friday when the matter was called up before Justice Roneiph Lawrence.

Hinson said the child’s Haitian mother, Fabienne Cherisma, who was recently arrested for overstaying her visa alongside her husband who is said to have used fraudulent documents to obtain Jamaican citizenship, were on Friday brought before the court so it could make a further order for the child to remain in the custody of the State.

However, Hinson said when the child was presented to the court, both parents went into shock.

“The child was taken to court with [healing] black and blue bruises under both eyes; what seemed to be burn marks to the right cheek and chin; swelling of the face, especially to the right cheek; and scratches to the nose. Both eyes were bloodshot in the corners. A medical shown to the court by the CPFSA officer who brought the baby to court, described the injuries as ‘non-accidental’,” Hinson told the Observer.

The attorney said that when the mother saw her child she “screamed and began to cry uncontrollably and the father collapsed. They had to be removed and later returned to the dock”.

Hinson said the court was also “visibly disturbed by the doctor’s findings and the injuries on the baby’s face”.

She said the CPFSA officer, when pressed by the judge about the cause of the child’s injuries, “informed the court that when she asked, on arriving to collect the child, she was told that he had hit his face on the crib”.

The attorney, in making a successful bail application on behalf of the mother, who was released on humanitarian grounds, however countered that, “both eyes were bruised and that could not have occurred if the child simply fell out his crib”.

“I also pointed out that the child is in danger where he is and that he needed his mother. My focus is really to get to the bottom of how the child received those injuries at Glenhope. Also, the bruises were healing and the burn mark almost completely healed. However, the child didn’t see a doctor until the day before court, on August 6, 2026. I need help in finding out when and how the child was injured and why the child wasn’t taken to the doctor until the day before the scheduled court date,” Hinson declared.

The attorney said she is in discussion with the child’s mother to determine the legal options available to her as she presses for answers regarding her son’s health. Hinson told the Observer that her client is adamant that the “child was in perfect health when removed from [their] home”.

The CPFSA issued a statement to the media on Monday saying “the incident is being investigated and is being treated with utmost urgency and importance”.

The agency stated that it “takes a zero-tolerance approach to all forms of child abuse” and said, based on the outcome of the investigation, it stands ready to execute all measures or sanctions regarding child abuse, in keeping with the Child Care and Protection Act (CCPA 2004).

Furthermore, the CPFSA said under its 2025–2027 strategic framework it established an islandwide initiative to equip residential child care facilities with security cameras, ensuring high safety standards are maintained across all locations.

“In light of the recent incident however, deployment has been prioritised to fast-track installation at the facility in which this incident has taken place,” the agency pledged.

World.title: Rock-born DJ Damage scores BMI Trailblazers award
World.content:
DJ Damage BMI Award.

JAMAICAN-BORN Leonard “DJ Damage” Douglas is celebrating career-defining achievements as the creative force behind Without You, a chart-topping single by Jevon Dewand and The Trap Starz.

The single, which reached #1 on Billboard’s Gospel Airplay Chart in February, was recognised as one of the year’s most-performed gospel songs at the Broadcast Music, Inc (BMI) Trailblazers of Gospel Music Awards on July 21 in Nashville, Tennessee.

The milestones are an international breakthrough for DJ Damage, whose two-decade career has taken him from Jamaica’s sound system culture to the global music stage.

The Atlanta-based DJ played a multidimensional role in the success of Without You, which is recognised as an urban, hip hop praise anthem, contributing as a songwriter, scratch DJ, producer, background vocalist, and featured performer in the accompanying music video.

The Billboard #1 capped an extraordinary 33-week run that saw Without You reshape the gospel and urban radio landscape, including a 12 per cent surge in radio spins during its climb to the top spot, and a #26 placement on the Billboard Year-End Top Gospel Airplay Chart.

“Reaching the Billboard #1 spot was nothing short of a dream come true. For a kid from Jamaica to achieve that level of recognition on one of music’s most prestigious charts is a milestone I don’t take lightly,” he said. “It represents both my personal achievement and a moment of pride for Jamaica and the Caribbean as a whole. Very few creatives from our region have ever stood at that height, and I’m deeply grateful and humbled to be among them.”

DJ Damage has built a career behind the scenes of the music industry, spinning for Grammy Award-winning R&B group 112; touring with American rap rock band Gym Class Heroes; and sharing stages with artistes including Swizz Beatz, DJ Khaled, Rick Ross, Ashanti, Sean Paul, Vybz Kartel, Mavado, Buju Banton, Beenie Man, and Bounty Killer.

Jevon Dewand credits DJ Damage’s versatility and musical instincts as key ingredients in the success of

Without You.

“He has a great ear for music. Sight is a blessing and vision is a gift. I saw the vision in him,” said Dewand. “DJ Damage knows all types of music, and he’s very versatile in all genres. Most DJs play music but can’t make it music. He can.”

While Billboard recognition and the BMI Award mark two of the biggest moments of his career, DJ Damage says the journey began in Prospect, Clarendon, where he first dreamt of making it in music. His breakthrough came years later in Stony Hill, St Andrew, when he convinced promoters to let him perform with R&B group 112.

“That night in Stony Hill was everything. It was me taking a chance and betting on myself. I knew that if I could just get my foot in the door and get on that stage with 112, my skills would reach the right ears,” he said.

They did.

“I still DJ for 112 to this day. From there I took the momentum to Jersey City and began DJ’ing with Gym Class Heroes, and it just kept building. Every connection, every show, and every risk led to the next opportunity. I went on to DJ for Shai, joined a sound system called Diamond Movements, and had the privilege of performing alongside legends across reggae, dancehall, R&B, hip hop, and more. That one night in Stony Hill set everything in motion.”

That momentum eventually led to an introduction from Wayne Wonder, which opened doors to King Promotions, touring opportunities with producer and songwriter Jazze Pha and, in 2023, performing before an audience of over 60,000 people during hip hop’s 50th anniversary celebration.

“It was electrifying. There’s really no other word to describe it. To me, standing on one of hip hop’s greatest stages, surrounded by some of the biggest names in the culture, celebrating 50 years of a genre that was born from Jamaican sound system culture, as a Jamaican DJ was priceless,” he said. “Every obstacle, every sacrifice, every door that was closed before one finally opened, all of it flashed in that moment. Not many DJs will ever have that experience. And standing there, I knew without a doubt that it was exactly where I was supposed to be. That feeling is truly indescribable.”

DJ Damage hopes his story encourages the next generation of creatives to dream bigger than their circumstances.

“These are moments I worked for over 20 years. I started with nothing but a chance and a will to prove myself. I hope young creatives across Jamaica and the Caribbean will see this win and know that if they have a dream and don’t know if it’s possible, it is.”

Following his latest achievements, DJ Damage will continue his momentum with a performance at the 41st Annual Stellar Gospel Music Awards on August 15 at the Spectrum Center in Charlotte, North Carolina. The awards ceremony will be later aired on BET.

World.title: Wellington praises Team Jamaica after World U-20 exploits
World.content:
Shanoya Douglas won three medals for Jamaica — gold in the women’s 4x100m relay and silver in the 100m and 200m. (Photo: Paul Reid)

OREGON, USA — Keith Wellington, team leader for Jamaica at the 21st staging of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships, says the team performed well despite the challenges of a long season.

Jamaica won eight medals — two gold, three silver and three bronze — to finish fourth on the medal table and third in the placing table with 89 points.

Hosts United States topped both tables with 24 medals —12 gold, seven silver and five bronze. Kenya were second with 11 medals — four gold, three silver and four bronze — while Italy finished third with five medals — three gold and two bronze.

Shanoya Douglas was Jamaica’s most successful athlete, winning three medals — gold in the women’s 4x100m relay and silver in the 100m and 200m.

Wellington said the performances were particularly impressive given that most of the athletes had been competing since January.

“I think under any circumstances this would be a really good performance,” Wellington told the Jamaica Observer on Sunday before the final two relays were contested. “Eight medals to date, and third in terms of quality.”

He said the overall standard at the championships had improved significantly.

“We have seen some really world-class standards, not just as juniors but the quality of the performances has been really, really good overall for all the countries. And so, to still be amongst the best, I think, we would be proud of the performances.”

Wellington singled out Michael Andre Edwards’ dramatic victory in the men’s triple jump during which he produced a World Under-20-leading and personal best 17.08m — the fifth-longest winning mark in the history of the event at the championships.

“Yeah, I think the obvious standout would be Team Captain Michael Andre’s performance. Not just the 17.08m but remember, you know, he took the lead with his second-to-last jump. It was taken away from him and he came back and claimed it. So it’s not just the result, but the quality and the performance there.”

He also highlighted the men’s discus throw competition on Sunday involving Jamaicans Joseph Salmon and Kamari Kennedy, when the lead changed several times over the final two rounds.

Jamaica also set two national records in the mixed 4x100m relay, which was contested for the first time at the championships, and the mixed 4x400m relay.

Ten Jamaicans produced personal bests, including Shevaughn Thomas and Sashane Johnson who each recorded two personal best performances.

Wellington said the athletes’ performances should not be judged solely by their results, pointing to the demands of the Jamaican school season.

“I think we don’t want to just look at the results, but look at the performances and you can see quite a few quality performances. And we cannot ignore, again, that our juniors have a really long season; and it is the schools that invest most in these kids, so they have to peak for champs because that is where the investment is,” he said.

“And so, for them to come back five months after their last performance for their schools again is sometimes a challenge that many of them have exams in the middle and all of that. So, I think it’s an incredible performance.”

World.title: STAYING PUT!
World.content:
Sanjay Seymore (left) anchors Jamaica’s men’s 4x100m relay team to victory in the semi-finals of the World Athletics Under-20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon, on Saturday. Jamaica ran 39.51 seconds to advance to the final. At centre is Hong Kong’s Cheuk Fung Jasper Koo, while at right is Australia’s Joshua John. (Photo: Paul A Reid)

OREGON, USA — William Knibb Memorial High School’s Sanjay Seymore has turned down several offers from United States colleges, choosing to remain in Jamaica as he targets places on the country’s teams for the 2027 World Athletics Championships and 2028 Olympic Games.

The ISSA/GraceKennedy Boys’ and Girls’ Athletics Championships and Carifta Games 200m champion is coming off a season of highs and lows, including finishing third in his favourite event at the Jamaica Athletics Administrative Association (JAAA) National Junior Championships and missing out on an individual spot on Jamaica’s team to the 21st World Athletics Under-20 Championships at Hayward Field in Eugene, Oregon.

Seymore, who recently signed a professional contract, declined to give details about his plans but confirmed to the Jamaica Observer on Sunday that he would remain in Jamaica for now.

“I can say definitely I’m staying in Jamaica for now. So yes, that’s the only thing I can say right now that I would be staying in Jamaica.”

He said he believes remaining at home gives him the best opportunity to make Jamaica’s teams for the World Championships and Olympics.

“It’s just I think it’s the best for me right now, I don’t really have anything against college,” he said. “I see that when you go college and then come back for the Jamaica trials, athletes are not at their best and then and you know we have World Championship and Olympics coming up.”

At 19, Seymore believes he has time to develop as he prepares to compete against some of the world’s leading sprinters, including Jamaica’s Oblique Seville.

“They already have their reputations, Oblique Seville is a world champion, so you can’t take that from him. So, as the rookie, I would say I’m just going into the big game with the seniors, and I’m just going to give it my best shot always, like I done in junior levels. But I know I have to put the best foot forward if I want to make it big as a Jamaican sprinter. So that’s definitely goal for me.”

Seymore had been expected to qualify for Jamaica’s team in the 200m but suffered an injury shortly before the JAAA Championships. He finished third in the final in 21.01 seconds behind Nathaniel Martin and Kyle Bodden.

He was subsequently added to the men’s 4x100m relay team and ran two strong anchor legs as Jamaica won bronze.

“After Carifta I had some injuries, went to trials and came third as I was coming back from the injury,” he said. “But I got my mind right and told myself I’m going to go on this relay and I’m going to give it my best shot and go into the best possible shape I can for the team.”

Seymore said he was pleased with his contribution to the bronze-medal effort.

“So I just went out there and give my best and we came short of the gold medal, but we still made the podium, so I’m pretty happy for that.”

World.title: BWE organisers respond to viral fight video, reaffirms commitment to patron safety
World.content:
Videograb showing a brawl at a Best Weekend Ever beach event on Sunday, August 10, 2026.

ST ANN, Jamaica – The directors of party series Best Weekend Ever (BWE) has expressed disappointment and regret over a physical altercation involving patrons at its beach event on Sunday.

Videos of the incident have been widely circulated on social media, showing a group of men engaged in a brawl.

In a media release Monday, the party organisers said, “Best Weekend Ever has never condoned, and we abhor the proliferation of violence of any kind at our events.

“We are extremely disappointed and sincerely regret that this unfortunate and isolated situation has occurred,” the release continued. “We have contacted the family of those affected and the individuals involved in the altercation have been clearly identified, and the relevant actions will be pursued by the designated authority.”

According to the directors, over the years, BWE has established a strong track record of providing safe, well-managed entertainment experiences for thousands of patrons.

“The safety and security of our guests remain a priority, and this incident is not reflective of the culture of Best Weekend Ever or the experience we work diligently to provide,” they said.

The directors also sought to clarify that, contrary to some narratives circulating, the MC at the event “brought attention to the incident to allow the appropriate intervention to take place and we have made our team available to the relevant authorities to assist in the process of ensuring this does not reoccur.”

According to the release, throughout the staging of Best Weekend Ever 2026, the events have been enjoyed safely by thousands of patrons with improved traffic management and movement between events.

“We are also grateful for the positive feedback from patrons which is an indication of the high level of satisfaction with the production of the event series,” the organisers said.

“Additional security measures have been put in place for the final event being staged today,” they added. “We thank our patrons, partners, security teams and stakeholders for their support as we continue to remain committed to delivering an environment where everyone can celebrate responsibly and safely.”

World.title: Swarming jellyfish overrun French nuclear plant on same date two years in a row
World.content:
Three fishing vessels are now “constantly patrolling off the coast of the plant" to conduct "preventive fishing operations [...] 24/7,” the company added.

Tuesday’s jellyfish invasion comes a the latest in a series of climate change-driven incidents that have affected French nuclear energy during a particularly infernal summer.

Nuclear power plants are typically built by rivers or on coastlines so they can use nearby water sources to cool their reactors. But a record number in France this summer have been forced to temporarily shut down due to heatwaves and droughts affecting their water supply.

Rising sea temperatures have made jellyfish swarms more common along the French coast in recent years, and those swarms can affect a plant’s ability to bring in seawater — which is what happened at Gravelines. Following last year’s incident at the plant along the North Sea, EDF installed cameras and deployed fishing boats to monitor the situation.

While the vessels “prevented a massive influx of jellyfish” on Saturday and Sunday, they were eventually overwhelmed as the swarm grew from “about 100 kilograms” to “several dozen tons,” the French state-owned utility giant said.

Opponents of nuclear energy were quick to jump on the incident.

“This only highlights that nuclear power plants are ill-equipped to deal with the consequences of climate change,” the French branch of Greenpeace said in statement.

World.title: Latvia discovers secret migrant tunnel at Belarus frontier
World.content:
Tunnels have previously been found in Lithuania, according to Baltic media, but this is the first time one has been used to cross into Latvia.

“This is the first case in which a tunnel has been used for illegal crossing of the state border into Latvia. No signs of violations had previously been detected in this exact location, and no detentions of persons illegally crossing the state border had occurred there,” Dombrava wrote on X.

Authorities returned all 15 people to their “country of departure” and are continuing to inspect the area around the tunnel.

Latvia launched an operation Tuesday to strengthen border security. Dombrava has described illegal border crossings from Belarus as a “hybrid threat.”

Authorities have prevented more than 9,000 illegal attempts to cross the border from Belarus so far this year, the Latvian State Border Guard said in a press release.

World.title: Putin used North Korean ballistic missiles in lethal attack on Ukraine, Zelenskyy says
World.content:
Russian President Vladimir Putin and North Korean ruler Kim Jong Un have deepened ties since the Kremlin’s war on Ukraine began. In September last year during a meeting in Beijing, Kim vowed to do “everything we can to assist Russia.”

Zelenskyy also reported attacks on a Kyiv hospital and businesses overnight, with at least one person injured. The capital’s mayor, Vitali Klitschko, urged residents late Monday to seek shelter.

Moscow also attacked substations in Kherson and Kharkiv, causing power outages, Zelenskyy said. Further attacks took place in the Donetsk, Dnipro and Mykolaiv regions.

“Every step Russia takes — increasing ballistic missile production, bringing in North Korean equipment, preparing for mobilization — all of this shows that Moscow is preparing not for peace, but for escalation,” Zelenskyy wrote.

Russia has stepped up its missile attacks this summer, with Zelenskyy urging Western allies to help Kyiv strengthen its air defenses and to heap sanctions pressure on companies fueling Moscow’s war. However, Europe is running out of Patriot interceptors to shoot down Russian missiles, according to the continent’s military officials.

Ukraine, meanwhile, has struck back, targeting Russian infrastructure including oil refineries and buildings belonging to e-commerce giant Wildberries.

Russian state media on Tuesday reported that two Wildberries warehouses in the Voronezh region, several hundred kilometers south of Moscow, caught fire following drone strikes, killing one person.

World.title: Trump backs Infantino after fury over FIFA chief’s World Cup sale plan
World.content:
FIFA President Gianni Infantino stands beside U.S. President Donald Trump with the World Cup trophy before presenting it to Spain after the final at New York New Jersey Stadium on July 19, 2026. | Dan Mullan/Getty Images

It would be a “terrible mistake” to replace the football boss after the success of the 2026 World Cup, the U.S. president posted on Truth Social.

U.S. President Donald Trump backed under-pressure football chief Gianni Infantino, after calls grew for the FIFA boss to quit following his aborted plan to sell off parts of the World Cup tournament to private investors.

“FIFA would be making a terrible mistake if, for any reason, they even considered replacing President Gianni Infantino. He is fantastic, having just presided over the most successful World Cup, by four times, ever presented,” Trump posted Tuesday morning on Truth Social.

Trump and Infantino cultivated a close relationship in the run-up to the 2026 World Cup, hosted this summer in North America, and the U.S. president helped present the trophy to victorious Spain in New Jersey in July.

World.title: Germany’s modern miracle: Churches are losing believers but gaining money
World.content:
Rising salaries have outweighed the cost of hundreds of thousands leaving the church.

German commentators are calling it a modern-day “miracle.”

Hundreds of thousands of worshippers in the country are walking away from their churches each year. The money, however, keeps rolling in.

Some 660,000 people formally quit the country’s Catholic and Protestant churches in 2025, freeing them from a levy automatically charged to registered members as a percentage of their income tax bill.

Despite the exodus, the two institutions collected more than €12.5 billion through the church tax for the 2025 fiscal year, up from around €12.4 billion in 2024.

The apparent miracle has a decidedly earthly explanation: Rising wages and Germany’s progressive tax system mean the shrinking pool of members is paying more.

“At first glance, the development may seem contradictory,” a spokesperson for the Evangelical Church in Germany — the umbrella organization representing Germany’s regional Protestant churches — said. “The reason is that church tax is calculated based on individual income tax.”





Members of Germany’s Catholic and Protestant churches and some Jewish communities pay an additional religious tax equal to 8 or 9 percent of their income tax liability, even if they don’t attend services.

In 2021, the most recent year for which comprehensive data is available, more than 29 million people paid church tax in Germany, amounting to almost half of all income taxpayers in Europe’s largest economy.

The German Finance Ministry’s 2025 payroll tax tables suggests that a single employee without children earning €50,000 gross a year pays approximately €600 in church tax annually on top of income tax, depending on the federal state. Someone earning €70,000 per year pays more than €1,000.

People are registered as part of their religious community at birth or at local government offices. To stop paying the church tax, they must formally leave through a process known as Kirchenaustritt, or “church exit.”

The procedure varies across Germany’s federal states but typically requires appearing in person at a registry office or local court to submit a declaration. Most states also charge an administrative fee.

While those who deregister can still attend services as a visitor and access some church services, they are not allowed to have a church wedding, be a godparent or be guaranteed a church burial.

In 2025, some 310,000 left the Catholic Church, while around 350,000 left one of Germany’s regional Protestant churches.

Church exit

The reasons people give for formally leaving their religious communities range from feeling less connected to the church to simply wanting to save money.

“People are leaving the Church because they feel it no longer plays a role in their lives,” said Matthias Kopp, director of communications for the German Bishops’ Conference.

“Added to this are the scandals of recent years, which have called the Church’s credibility into question,” he added. “There are also people — though this is by no means the primary reason — who leave the Church because of the church tax.”

“These are processes of alienation to which we must respond,” said Kopp.

For Jana Keil, a 33-year-old accountant from Berlin, the decision was both financial and moral. “I no longer wanted to support the system with church tax in light of the [child sex] abuse scandals,” she said.





Lukas Heinich, a 23-year-old working student, said he formally left after completing his apprenticeship because he “didn’t feel like paying the tax or supporting the church.”

That church tax revenues continue to rise despite the exodus is down to the types of taxpayers choosing to remain church members.

Those who are still paying church tax in Germany are “probably the higher earners,” said Zareh Asatryan, professor of empirical economics at the University of Münster. “Those that stay will naturally earn more income because of inflation plus real wage growth, and they will just generate more revenue.”

A miracle with an end date?

But the continued rise in church tax revenue masks significant long-term challenges — and raises questions about how long the trend can last.

While those revenues are going up, they are “relatively sluggish” and “haven’t been increasing by a lot,” said Asatryan.

The increase in revenue from the church tax is considerably lower than the increase in revenue from income tax. State revenue from wage and income taxes rose by 6.65 percent in 2025, said Kopp, whereas church tax revenue increased by 1.93 percent.

“Long-term projections indicate that church tax revenue will decline significantly over the coming decades as church membership continues to decrease,” said the spokesperson for the Evangelical Church in Germany.

Protestant churches are already preparing for their income to decrease “through long-term planning processes,” said the spokesperson. “Without this system, the church’s religious, social and charitable work would not be possible on its current scale.”

World.title: EU opens channel with Meta, TikTok to tackle Ceuta migrant crisis
World.content:
That will serve as a point of contact for platforms, fact-checkers and the Commission to quickly flag content so that it can be reviewed and taken down if necessary. The effort comes amid concerns that disinformation is promoting further crossings into the territory on Aug. 15, according to Maldita.es. Maldita.es and the European Fact-Checking Standards Network attended Monday’s meeting.

The Commission operates a rapid response system under its code of conduct on disinformation, often triggered around elections. The new mechanism on Ceuta would bring a closer group of stakeholders together, two of the people said.

Another meeting has been set for later this week, one of those people and the third person confirmed.

Meta and TikTok said they were already actively monitoring the situation in line with their policies and had set up dedicated teams to monitor and respond to content in real time.

The crisis has divided EU countries and has reignited Europe’s long-running debate on illegal migration. Italy has since been one of the harshest critics of Spain’s left-wing government and its migration policies, and has implemented border controls for travelers arriving from Spain.

Former EU commissioner Thierry Breton, who was a force behind the EU’s online content rules, on Monday said the bloc should launch a disinformation inquiry into the Ceuta crisis in an interview with Italian newspaper La Stampa.

World.title: Greece’s aging power grid blamed for catastrophic wildfires
World.content:
Two deadly wildfires in late July — one in western Attica and one on the island of Crete —were also linked to the electricity grid in preliminary findings from the Greek fire brigade. The fires destroyed more than 36,000 acres and killed four people.

“Six out of 10 major fires and 55 percent of the area burnt in 2025 were caused by the power grid,” said Elias Tziritis, wildfires actions coordinator at World Wildlife Fund Greece. “Statistically speaking, the majority of fires may not start from the power grid, but these are the ones that cause the most major, devastating fires.”

Loose or sagging power lines, vegetation coming in contact with cables, dust buildup on transmission equipment and other such faults can all generate sparks. The risk rises during strong winds and periods of heavy electricity demand, when aging infrastructure is under greater strain.

Much of Greece’s electricity grid was installed decades ago and runs above ground through fire-prone forests and increasingly depopulated rural areas. In the 1960s, the country opted for an overhead network as a cheaper way to extend electricity across the country, while the prolonged financial crisis that began in 2009 further constrained investment in the system.

Critics say Greece has moved too slowly to bury distribution lines and adapt the network to increasingly severe fire conditions.

“We raised the issue years ago, calling for something to be done with the power grid urgently,” said Christos Kalogeropoulos, a retired lieutenant-general with the Fire Service and former director of the Arson Crimes unit. “We have been calling for urgent underground cabling.”
